note: 161,000 sq ft federally funded athletic complex begun fall 2001; its 23,000 sq ft varsity weight room (used by football, hockey, basketball and others) opened January 2003, and the 2004 release mentions coaches' offices. Football's locker room is in Falcon Stadium. Cost not found. A later $1.2M weight room upgrade is below the $3M line.

92,000 sq ft privately funded building with a regulation football field, also used by lacrosse and soccer. Ground broke October 2010; dedicated July 22, 2011, in use from fall 2011. $19M construction cost per Athletic Business; lead gift $5M from Bart and Lynn Holaday.

project: Falcon Stadium football locker room complex renovation
note: Before the 2018 season the home locker room was completely rebuilt with new medical rooms, a coaches' room and a media room; the complex grew by more than 9,000 sq ft over the old 3,875 sq ft. Mostly privately funded. Cost not found (likely over $3M given the size, not confirmed).

The infobox names HKS as architect and structural engineer for the 2024 renovations, and capacity fell from 46,692 to 39,441 from 2024. The article does not say what was built or what it cost. Team spaces are not mentioned.

project: Louis and Freda Stile Athletics Field House
note: 155,500 sq ft field house built 2004 beside the Student Recreation Center: 120-yard indoor football field inside a 300m track, the strength and conditioning center, varsity locker rooms and football's offices (Wikipedia, Akron Zips football). Serves all 19 sports. Its own cost was not found: the combined rec center and field house is listed at $40M, and a 1999 plan had a $6M field house, so cost left unknown.

New stadium replacing the Rubber Bowl; $61.6M includes the end zone facility. Groundbreaking Feb or Apr 2008 (infobox and text differ), opened Sep 12, 2009. The athletics site says the end zone facility's first floor holds a team meeting and locker room for the Zips (also used by high schools), so team_spaces true. Football's offices, main weight room and indoor field are in the Stile Athletics Field House, so it does not house football operations.

project: Football Building (now Mal M. Moore Athletic Facility)
note: Per the 2007 UA dedication release it opened in 1986 as the Football Building. Renamed for Mal Moore in 2007. Also holds athletics administration.
Finished October 1986, named for Crisp in 1991. About 97,000 sq ft. A 2016 renovation removed the tennis area (cost not found).
Added about 10,000 seats. Alabama played its 1987 home games at Legion Field while this was built. Cost not found.
Approved in 1995. Final cost $35M. Capacity went to 83,818.

project: Bryant-Denny Stadium north end zone expansion
note: About $47M after the 2004 season, finished in 2006. Upper deck and skyboxes. Groundbreaking year not stated.

project: Bryant-Denny Stadium south end zone expansion
note: Budget was $80.6M; it came in at about $65.6M. Work began early 2009 and finished mid-2010. Upper deck, 36 skyboxes, club seats.

project: Football strength and conditioning facility (weight room)
note: New 37,000 sq ft weight room at the football building, opened January 2013.
Planned $92.5M (a 2018 headline said $75M). Added a new game-day locker room reached by an extended Walk of Champions tunnel, plus premium seats. Work began just after the 2019 season.

project: Mal M. Moore Athletic Facility renovation and Sports Science addition
note: Ran Nov 2019 to Aug 2020: new locker room, training room, lobby and sports science addition. UA lists a $16M budget; an engineering firm cites $20M.

project: Sofield Family Indoor Practice Facility (original, about 50 yards)
note: The existing indoor building near Kidd Brewer Stadium, described as a 2007 facility nearing the end of its life with a field of only about 50 yards; football still splits offense and defense in bad weather. Cost not found; opening year from the 2024-25 replacement reports, not confirmed elsewhere.

project: Kidd Brewer Stadium west-side complex (KBS Complex) and east upper deck
note: 100,000 sq ft complex behind the home stands with strength and conditioning, athletic training, hydrotherapy, locker rooms and offices for all sports, plus suites and club seats. The east upper deck opened in 2008 and the complex in 2009. $32M is the infobox figure for the 2008 expansion; the work was part of a $50M athletics facilities campaign. Groundbreak taken from the press box coming down after the 2006 season.

project: Kidd Brewer Stadium North End Zone complex (replaced Owens Field House)
note: $45M budget. Athletic training, hydrotherapy, locker rooms, nutrition, coaches' and athletics offices, ticketing, and about 1,000 seats. Construction ran 2019 to spring 2021; it opened for the 2021 opener.

project: New Sofield Family Indoor Practice Facility
note: About 85,000-106,000 sq ft multipurpose building next to Kidd Brewer Stadium with a full 100-yard field, for football and most other sports. Ceremonial groundbreaking Aug 15, 2025 (work already under way). Reported at $29M; an April 2026 report (wataugaonline.com) headlined $25M. Turf in; App State says use starts fall 2026 with full completion December 2026.

project: Arizona Stadium north end zone seats, press box and sky boxes
note: Permanent north end zone seats added in 1988. A new press box with 23 suites and 319 loge seats was built after the 1988 season. Seating and premium only. No cost found.

Four-story, 187,000 sq ft football HQ in the north end zone: locker room, weight room, training room, offices, meeting rooms and cafeteria, plus 4,200 seats and suites on top. Broke ground after the 2011 season (one Daily Wildcat report says Dec 2011). Team moved in July 2013. Some outlets say $72M or $75M; Mortenson's construction contract was $56.9M.
Lower east concourse, restrooms, concessions and student section, part of a $66M athletics capital plan approved Sept 2017. Reported as $25,463,000 or about $25M. Fan amenities only.

project: Cole and Jeannie Davis Sports Center
note: Indoor practice building with a 90-yard turf field next to two 80-yard outdoor fields, east of the stadium. Construction began April 2018. Unveiled Feb 24, 2019. Earlier figures were $15M-18M; Mortenson lists $14.8M.

project: Lowell-Stevens Football Facility remodel (weight room, offices, locker room)
note: Remodel in Jedd Fisch's first year: new weight room, coaching offices, rehab equipment and locker room. About $6M comes from one Tucson newspaper report and is not confirmed elsewhere.

Athletics department building at the stadium's south end. Wikipedia says it was added 'during that time' around the 1988 seat addition, so the year is uncertain. It held the football offices until the 2017 north end facility opened. Not confirmed whether it held the football locker or weight room.

Air-supported indoor practice bubble at the Kajikawa fields. Broke ground May 15, 2008. A storm brought it down on Aug 28, 2008, before handover. It was re-inflated in Oct 2008 and fully repaired for use in July 2009.

project: Student-Athlete Facility (north end zone, Sun Devil Stadium)
note: Football building at the stadium's north end: offices, meeting rooms, study rooms and support space. Size is given as 85,000 or 115,000 sq ft. Its cost is part of the stadium renovation row. The sources I read do not name the locker or weight room.

Five-year rebuild in phases: upper deck cut and south end in 2015, west side in 2016, north end facility and video board in 2017, east side in 2018, clubs in 2019. Work began after the 2014 season. Other totals cited are $268M and more than $300M. team_spaces is false here only because the football spaces it built are the separate Student-Athlete Facility row; this cost includes that building.
Indoor practice facility built in 1998. A 1998 Talk Business item says it cost about $3M. Now part of the Walker Family Training Center.
Grew from about 51,000 to 72,000 permanent seats. Wikipedia's infobox gives $106M; the 1998 plan was $65M. No team spaces mentioned.
80,000 sq ft. Groundbreaking set for Nov 4, 2011; opened summer 2013. Early estimates were $28M for the building and $35M with practice fields; later reports say about $40M.

project: Razorback Stadium north end zone addition
note: Approved June 2016. Broyles Athletic Center was torn down in the 2016-17 offseason to make room. Added a new game-day locker room, training room and suites.
Original stadium, $2.5M. First game 1974, finished before the 1975 season. No sourced details on team spaces.

project: Indian Stadium expansion for the move to Division I-A
note: Double-decked grandstand and a four-level press and donor area; capacity went to 30,708. Seating and press box only.

project: 2002 stadium renovation: players' and coaches' complex with Performance Enhancement Center
note: Added luxury suites and a new complex with coaches' offices, dressing rooms, meeting rooms and player lounges, plus a Performance Enhancement Center (athletic training, strength and conditioning, academic center). No cost found.

project: Centennial Expansion (press box and west concourse)
note: Press box grew from 7,120 to 36,000 sq ft, with new concourse, restrooms and ticketing. Funded by a $5M Johnny Allison gift; the total cost was not given. Built in the nine months between the 2014 and 2015 seasons.

project: Student Activity Center (football indoor practice field)
note: 78,000-80,000 sq ft building with a full indoor football field that serves as the football team's indoor practice facility and as student recreation space. Construction began spring 2014, completed August 2015, ribbon cut September 2015. $11M estimate covered the center and relocating the soccer complex.

project: Centennial Bank Athletics Operations Center (north end zone football building)
note: Two-level, about 58,000-66,500 sq ft football operations building in Centennial Bank Stadium's north end zone, beside the indoor field: locker room, weight room, sports medicine and staff offices. Work began late 2017 with removal of the north end zone bleachers; the team moved in before the 2019 opener. $29M budget, privately funded ($5M each from Centennial Bank and the Allison family). Replaces the 2002 complex as football's home.

project: Kimsey Athletic Center (Michie Stadium south end)
note: 120,000 sq ft four-story building at Michie Stadium's south end: 20,000 sq ft strength center, athletic training, locker rooms, coaches' offices, meeting rooms, equipment and media rooms. Football's main home. $40M, completed spring 2003; a West Point alumni page shows construction under way in May 2001 (groundbreak year not confirmed). Phase I of the 'Margin of Excellence' upgrade.

Indoor building (77,000-92,000 sq ft, sources differ) with a full 100-yard field and end zones; ribbon cutting March 2007. Phase II of the 'Margin of Excellence' upgrade, funded by a $15M gift from Bill and Carol Foley; construction cost not stated.

project: Michie Stadium Preservation Project (east grandstand replacement)
note: Construction began April 15, 2024. It replaces the east stands, walkways, restrooms and concessions, adds premium hospitality and end-zone-to-end-zone cadet seating. The infobox lists it as renovated in 2026 with capacity 35,647. No team spaces mentioned. Cost not found.
Capacity went to 85,214. Cost not found.
100,000 sq ft, opened June 1989. Held athletics offices and football operations until the Woltosz center. A later $5M locker and training room renovation is undated.
Dedicated Sept 4, 1999. Only a 40-yard indoor field. Later converted into an Olympic-sport weight room.

project: Jordan-Hare Stadium east upper deck extensions and suites
note: Added sections at both ends of the east upper deck plus suites; capacity 87,451. Cost not found.
Approved June 2010; moved in August 2011. 92,000 sq ft. Budget reported as $16-16.5M; Athletic Business lists a $12.5M construction cost.
Southwest corner. Renovated and expanded the home locker room, moved the press box, added a recruiting lounge and a club. Built instead of the dropped $145M north end zone plan.

project: Jordan-Hare Stadium press box club and coaches' box renovation
note: Premium club seats and a lounge in the west upper deck press box. Coaches' and TV boxes renovated.
Groundbreaking Aug 21, 2021; grand opening January 2023. Total $91.9M (about $92M). One report counts 138,100 sq ft of operations space plus a 95,300 sq ft indoor practice facility.
About 106,000 sq ft with turf and room for offense and defense side by side. The AD said $9M, on budget. The team was practicing inside by late Oct 2003. Announced Sept 2002.

project: LaVell Edwards Stadium 2003 renovation (club and Legacy seating)
note: Added luxury club seating and Legacy Seats on the east side, cutting capacity to 64,045. Premium seating only. No cost published.

Building for all student-athletes that holds the football locker room, weight room and offices. About $21M before opening, out of roughly $50M raised for the complex (with the IPF and a $19M endowment). Completion was set for Nov 2003; later sources give 2004 as the opening.
2,500 sq ft extension with 10 racks on the north end of the weight room, ready for fall camp 2016. BYU, a private school, does not disclose costs, and it may be under $3M.
First locker room overhaul since the SAB opened, paid from the building's endowment. Work was underway April 2021 and unveiled June 2021. BYU does not disclose the cost.

Expanded football offices: a defensive meeting room, three position rooms and a recruit meeting space, plus the Built4Life Center. Announced April 2023 for completion by Aug 2023; completion not confirmed. Cost not disclosed.
New grass surface, LED lights and an improved players' entrance before the 2024 season. No team rooms. Cost unknown.

Football training building at Scheumann Stadium, completed 2001 and named for John and Janice Fisher in 2005. Contents and cost were not found in what I saw; the Venderly Center (offices) and the indoor facility were later built against it.
$13M renovation finished 2007: lights, north end zone lawn seating enclosure (22,500 horseshoe), concessions, brick facade, bigger press box, suites. No team spaces named.

project: Ron and Joan Venderly Football Center
note: 12,633 sq ft addition on the west side of the Fisher complex: 140-seat team meeting theater, coaches' offices, staff meeting room and recruiting lounge. Ground broke June 19, 2014; slated for the 2015 season, formally dedicated September 2016. Part of the $20M Cardinal Commitment campaign; its own cost not found.

About 87,000 sq ft privately funded indoor field next to the Fisher complex, on the old grass practice fields. $15M approved May 2019; construction began June 2020; football used it for spring camp April 2021, ribbon cutting Oct 2, 2021.

project: Floyd Casey Stadium renovation and Carl and Thelma Casey Athletic Center
note: An $8M renovation, $5M of it from Carl Casey; the stadium was renamed in 1988. The Casey Athletic Center opened in 1991 with locker rooms, training rooms and weight facilities. Wikipedia gives 1989 as the renovation year. The stadium closed in 2013, so this row is history only.

project: Floyd Casey Stadium west side press box and luxury suites
note: New press box with 20-24 suites on the west side. Premium seating only. The stadium closed in 2013.

project: Simpson Athletics and Academic Center (with Highers Athletics Complex)
note: About 96,000 sq ft football HQ: locker room, weight room, coaches' offices, meeting rooms, training room and academic center. $34M covers it plus the Highers outdoor practice complex. Broke ground May 2007 and was dedicated Dec 2008 (Wikipedia says 2009).

project: Jay and Jenny Allison Indoor Football Practice Facility
note: 100-yard indoor field. Broke ground Nov 15, 2008, finished Sept 2009, dedicated Sept 26, 2009. Cost figures conflict: about $11M estimated (Baylor), $10M on the Texas state registry, and an uncited $15.4M on Wikipedia.
New on-campus stadium on the Brazos. It includes a 7,500 sq ft home locker room. First game Aug 31, 2014.

New football operations building joined to the Allison indoor facility. The Regents approved a total budget of $89.6M; about $90M is reported as the finish cost. Groundbreaking was planned by summer 2022, but the exact date is not confirmed. The team moved in Aug 19, 2024, and it was dedicated Sept 27, 2024.
For the move to Division I-A, the two-tier stands were extended around the south end zone corners, taking capacity to 30,000 in 1997. No cost given.
The indoor practice facility just northwest of the stadium. The article says it officially opened Feb 2006. No cost given.

Three-story west side complex: press box, suites, loge boxes and club seats, with capacity up to 32,000. Construction began Feb 11, 2007 and it opened Aug 27, 2008. No cost on Wikipedia. Premium seating only.

project: Albertsons Stadium permanent end zone bleachers
note: Permanent bleachers in the north and south end zones before the 2012 season, taking capacity to about 36,387-37,000. Seating only.

project: North end zone football complex (Bleymaier Football Center)
note: The 2010 plan's first stage was a north end zone building for football offices, weight room, training room, equipment room and locker room. A revised version broke ground Apr 2012 and was finished by June 2013. The article does not name the building; Bleymaier Football Center is the usual name. No cost given (the whole plan was about $100M).

About 12,000 to 12,500 seats added, for 44,500. BC's athletics site says work began early 1994. Cost not found. Wikipedia also mentions a 1988 rebuild with upper decks and a press box. A premium-seating renovation was announced in 2025-26 for the 2026 season; it is left out because no start by the end of 2025 was confirmed.

Holds football offices, weight room, sports medicine and locker room, behind the north end zone. BC gives $27M and a March 2005 move-in. Athletic Business and GlobeSt give $17M construction cost, and Wikipedia says it opened Feb 2003; the BC figures are better supported.
115,700 sq ft. Full indoor football field plus a 12,000 sq ft strength and conditioning center. Opened July 2018. Part of a roughly $200M athletics plan. Groundbreaking date not found (likely 2017).

project: Barry Gallup '69 Sports Medicine Center (football sports medicine renovation)
note: A privately funded renovation of football's sports medicine center, set to open August 2021. It also added a nutrition and hydration area in the locker room. No cost was disclosed. A BC page also mentions a major locker room renovation before the 2015 season, cost not given.

Built 1992 for $8.7M; has a turf room and a track room; LED lights 2015. The source says it was built to promote intramural sports and does not say football practices there; football use is from general knowledge, not confirmed by a source read.
Described only as an extensive remodel in 1997 for $2M; contents unknown, so team_spaces false.

project: Sebo Center (Doyt Perry Stadium north end zone)
note: Enclosed the north end zone for 2007: band seating, suites, offices, training facilities, box office; FieldTurf put in the same year. Cost not found. team_spaces true because it holds offices and training facilities.
New stadium, groundbreaking Sep 17, 1991, opened Sep 4, 1993, $23M, HOK Sport. Whether it holds the team's own spaces was not stated, so team_spaces false.
Rounded bleacher sections in the south and north end zones raised capacity above 29,000; seating only. The north bleachers were torn down in 2017 to make room for the field house.

92,000 sq ft, $18M, state approval June 2017, work started October 2017 north of the stadium; it was the last MAC school to get one. The opening year 2018 is an estimate: no source I read gives it. Cost is the approved figure.

project: Simpson Center for Student-Athlete High Performance
note: 142,000 sq ft beside the stadium's west wall. Home of football (locker rooms, offices, meeting rooms, training and sports medicine) and 12 Olympic sports. The cost rose from a $111.9M estimate to $153M. Construction started in late 2008 after the oak grove court rulings. Berkeley says 2011; one vendor page says 2012.

project: California Memorial Stadium seismic retrofit and renovation
note: The west side was demolished and rebuilt, with fault-rupture blocks and a lowered field. Work ran June 2010 to Sept 2012, and Cal played 2011 at AT&T Park. The team's own spaces are in the Simpson Center, listed separately.
New stadium, groundbreaking Sep 1971, dedicated Nov 4, 1972, about 20,000 seats, $2.2M. The original team spaces were not described, so team_spaces false.

80,000 sq ft, $27M per the athletics site; dedicated at a home football game Sep 12, 1998 (the site lists 1999 as opening). Holds coaches' offices, the varsity weight room, meeting rooms, academic center and a full indoor FieldTurf field, joined to the stadium locker room by a tunnel. Listed separately from the $28M stadium expansion of the same years; whether the two figures overlap was not confirmed.

$28M project after the 1997 season: 10,000 seats (to 30,199), two-tier press box, a locker room, nine suites. The source says only 'following the 1997 season', so the 1998 opening is inferred. Football's locker, training and equipment rooms are now in the north end zone.

project: Chippewa Champions Center (Kelly/Shorts north end zone)
note: About 50,000-54,000 sq ft building at the north end of Kelly/Shorts Stadium, opened September 2020: 4,200 sq ft football locker room, 7,000 sq ft football weight room with strength staff offices, training and equipment rooms, plus a 4,000 sq ft VIP club. $22M per the university; BD+C says $30M and a 2018 estimate was $27M. Groundbreak year not found.

46,150 sq ft football field house at the stadium's southeast end, with athletic and academic spaces, plus 145,000 sq ft of grass practice fields. Construction finished fall 2012. Its cost is inside the stadium's $45M project, so it has no separate figure.

New on-campus stadium, ground broken April 28, 2011. Finished October 2012, first game August 31, 2013. Built in one project with the Judy W. Rose Football Center (separate row) and practice fields. The board approved $40.5M in bonds for the stadium and field house.

project: Jerry Richardson Stadium west-side press and suite tower expansion
note: Approved April 18, 2024 at $60M; a later Axios headline cited in the article says $70M. Adds a press and suite tower, premium seats, an upper deck (18,170 capacity) and a dedicated team dining facility with meeting space, hence team_spaces true. The article only says construction was slated to begin August 2025, so whether ground actually broke in 2025 is not confirmed. Completion was expected early 2027.

The stadium closed for renovation (UC played 1990 at Riverfront). Phase I in 1991 fortified the structure and added a three-tier press box. Phase II in 1992 expanded the east upper deck to about 35,000 seats. No cost found.

project: Nippert Stadium north end zone gameday locker rooms
note: New gameday locker rooms behind the north end zone, under the new Campus Rec Center, plus a north end zone grandstand and a bigger video board. No cost found.

Athletics HQ with coaches' offices, including football, and strength and conditioning facilities. Grand opening May 2006. No cost for the Lindner Center alone was found: $105M (or $116M, with $109M fixed construction) is the whole Varsity Village, which also built Marge Schott baseball stadium (2004) and other venues.
About 100,000 sq ft indoor facility. Construction cost $13.5M; occupied Aug 2011. Later razed: the 2025 Sheakley complex stands on its site.

New west pavilion with press box, suites, loges and club seats, plus wider concourses. First estimated at $70M, later budgeted at $86M. Construction from Dec 2013 to Sept 2015; UC played 2014 at Paul Brown Stadium.

One 210,000 sq ft complex: an 84,000 sq ft indoor building with a 120-yard field (used by all 18 UC teams) and a 96,000 sq ft Athletics Performance Center for football operations (strength and conditioning, locker rooms, physical therapy, offices, team meeting rooms; dining for all athletes). The $134M covers the whole complex, which is listed only here. Broke ground May 2023; ribbon cut June 11, 2025.

project: WestZone Phase 1 (Memorial Stadium west end zone)
note: Closed in the west end zone, added luxury boxes and club seats, and fully renovated the locker rooms. A 2006 report said the cost rose to $40M from a $27M estimate. A final figure was not confirmed.

project: WestZone Phase 2 (football offices, meeting rooms, strength and training)
note: Moved all football offices and team meeting rooms from the McFadden Building into the WestZone, with dedicated football training and strength rooms, before the 2009 season. A 2006 report put it at almost $20M. Construction was underway in 2008.

80,000 sq ft with a full football field. Ground broke March 2012 and it was dedicated Jan 25, 2013. A 12,000 sq ft addition (photo, video and NIL studios, about $4.5M approved) opened in early 2023; it is not listed separately because it is not team space.

project: WestZone Phase 3 (Oculus entrance, museum, northwest concourse)
note: Part of the $50M plan announced Jan 2011. The northwest concourse started April 2011 and was done for the 2011 season. The Oculus, the final piece, was finished in 2015. No team spaces.

About 142,000 sq ft (other figures say 145,000 to 159,500). Opened Feb 1, 2017 after about 13 months of building; construction started Dec 2015. A $4.8M performance and wellness addition was approved later; its date is unclear.

project: Memorial Stadium renovation Phase I (videoboard, premium clubs, west end zone)
note: Trustees approved about $68.7M in Oct 2019 (also reported as about $67M). The pandemic pushed completion from 2021 to 2022. Locker rooms were moved to Phase II.

project: Memorial Stadium renovation Phase II (home locker room and tunnel)
note: Gameday locker room renovated and expanded to nearly 8,000 sq ft, with a new tunnel, finished Aug 2023. The board approved a $65M Phase 2 that covered more than the locker room, so the locker room's own cost is unknown.
New stadium with 6,408 seats; groundbreak July 30, 2002, dedicated September 6, 2003. The infobox's $59M looks like a cumulative figure, so the original cost is left unknown. No sourced team spaces.

project: Adkins Fieldhouse (now Marrio & Josh Norman Fieldhouse)
note: North end zone building, opened June 2010. Football offices, meeting rooms and locker room, a 13,000 sq ft strength center for all athletes, other sports' offices, and 1,600 seats.

project: Brooks Stadium expansion phase I (to 15,000 seats)
note: Groundbreak March 21, 2017; ready for the September 2017 opener. The $38M bond figure covers both phases. Seating and press box upper deck only.

project: Brooks Stadium expansion phase II (west upper deck and premium seating)
note: Started January 2018, finished August 2019; capacity over 20,000. Its cost is inside the $38M project total on the phase I row.
93,000 sq ft; ribbon cutting June 2025. $15M is the 2021 estimate when Joe Moglia's gift started design work; final cost not found. Groundbreak year not found.

92,000 sq ft privately funded center at Folsom Field's north end; ground broke December 1990, ready for football by mid-August 1991, rest finished that fall. Football's home (locker room, weight room, offices) until the Champions Center, to which it is now linked by a bridge; also served the athletic department. $14M from one CU Athletics article only.

project: Folsom Field east side suites and club seats
note: Suites and club seating on the east side; capacity rose to 53,750. Premium seating only. No cost found.

project: Champions Center (high-performance sports center) and north end zone rebuild
note: $156M covers the whole initiative: the indoor practice facility, the Champions Center (the new home of CU football and athletic administration, with locker rooms, dining and lounge; completed February 2016), Dal Ward renovations, northeast corner seats, and a north end zone rebuilt with boxes and club seats before the 2016 season. Earlier figure $143M; one engineer lists $177M.

project: Indoor practice facility (2014-16 Folsom Field project)
note: Part of the expansion started in 2014. Its cost is in the $156M on the Champions Center row. CU Athletics in March 2015 projected completion in January 2016, and it opened in time for spring practice 2016.
cost_in: Champions Center (high-performance sports center) and north end zone rebuild

note: A $15.2M renovation for fall 2005 that added club seats and 12 luxury suites. Hughes was replaced in 2017 and no longer serves the team. Premium seating only.

About 62,000-66,000 sq ft, with a 70-yard synthetic turf football field and a basketball/volleyball court. A 2010 CSU article calls it the new $13M Indoor Practice Facility; CSU's facilities page says it was established in 2009. The football team uses it in bad weather and for spring practice.

New on-campus stadium, with construction from May 2015 (ceremony Sept 2015) and opening Aug 5, 2017; first game Aug 26, 2017. It cost $220.1M against an early $246M estimate. CSU's facilities page says the building holds the football locker room, a 9,100 sq ft weight room (another CSU listing says 8,807), a 150-seat team meeting room, position rooms and the football staff offices. So the team's whole home is inside it (the 2017 player reveal: csurams.com/news/2017/7/17/new-facilities-revealed-to-csu-football-players).

project: Delaware Field House conversion to indoor turf practice facility
note: The 1966 field house (indoor track, tennis and basketball until 1992) was converted in 2013 into an indoor practice facility. It got artificial turf for all sports, football included: a 70-yard indoor turf field with about 500 seats. No cost found. An $80M north end zone building with offices and indoor practice space has been talked about, but no groundbreaking was found.

project: Delaware Stadium renovation (west stands, press box, club level)
note: Part of the same $60M campaign as the Whitney Athletic Center. New home-side seating was ready Aug 2019; press box, club and concessions were finished by Dec 2020. Fan areas only.

A two-story building of 88,617-90,000 sq ft beside Delaware Stadium, holding a 10,000 sq ft strength and conditioning area that football shares (it replaced a 3,000 sq ft weight room), athletic training, nutrition and academic space, with the stadium press box on its top floor. The ceremonial groundbreaking was Dec 18, 2018, for the combined $60M Whitney center and stadium renovation (the Whitney family gave $10M). The contractor lists it as completed Sept 2020; some UD items say it fully opened in 2021. The $60M covers both projects and can't be split, so cost stays unknown. Sources don't say whether the football locker room and offices are inside it.

Holds the weight room, meeting rooms and home locker room, with a tunnel to Wallace Wade Stadium. Construction began Nov 2000 and it was dedicated Oct 2002. Duke releases say $20M, a 2009 Chronicle story says $23M, and the 2000 approval was $18M; $22M is the most cited.

80,000 sq ft with a 120-yard field at the Brooks Practice Facility. Dedicated Sept 2, 2011, and under construction in April 2011. The $6M Pascal lead gift was part of $10M pledged in 2009 for the practice facilities. Total cost not found.

project: Wallace Wade Stadium renovation (track removal, Blue Devil Tower)
note: Work began Dec 1, 2014: the track was removed, the field lowered, and a tower with 21 suites, 516 club seats and a press box built. The third phase finished before 2017. About $100M is the common figure, but Duke tied it to athletics upgrades across campus; WUNC reported $85M.

project: Yoh Football Center locker room and first-floor renovation
note: About 17,550 sq ft: locker room, recruiting and player lounges, nutrition center, nap room. It took about eight months and was unveiled July 2024. Donor-funded, cost withheld. Wikipedia says Yoh renovations began in 2022.

Three-story, 80,283 sq ft building next to the stadium, built 1989. Holds coaches' offices, the football locker room, the athletic training room, the equipment room, and eight football meeting rooms (a 107-seat team room and position rooms).

project: Dowdy–Ficklen Stadium north upper deck and club level
note: North upper deck finished 1998 (capacity 40,000), north club level (3,000 seats) in 1999, with press box improvements. A $2M scoreboard followed in 1999. Cost of the deck not found.

52,475 sq ft building in the west end zone; opened to athletes June 2002 and dedicated September 13, 2002. Football's strength and conditioning area is on the ground floor; it also has a banquet hall and an academic center.
Fully renovated in 2005; three fields (two Bermuda grass, one FieldTurf). Cost not found, so it may fall under the $3M threshold.

project: Dowdy–Ficklen Stadium east end zone expansion
note: Began December 2009. Added 7,000 east end zone seats (capacity 50,000), an HD scoreboard and chairback seats.

The program article says $55M, the stadium article $60M. A four-story south tower with suites, loge boxes and club seats, a new press box and a field-level club; it opened August 2019. Construction began after the 2017 season (exact groundbreaking year not given). The plans also listed improvements to the Ward Sports Medicine Building and Scales Field House for athletes, but no details, so team_spaces is false.
Seats extended south from each grandstand to meet Division I-A minimum size rules. Seating only.

Ground broke Oct 2009, finished in the 2009-10 academic year (so opened 2010 is inferred). Air-supported; also used by soccer, baseball, softball and golf. Cost from the cited AnnArbor.com headline ($3.9M).

project: Rynearson Stadium renovation (Crosby Field, track removed)
note: New playing surface; the track around the field removed and a separate track built. Linked to Maxx Crosby's $1M gift; the total cost was not found. No team spaces named.
7,500-seat football and track stadium, $3M. Ground broke July 1994; opened Sept 1995. Football only started in 2002, when movable bleachers raised it to 17,000.

project: FIU Stadium rebuild, phase one (with Landon Field House)
note: Most of the 1995 stadium was torn down and rebuilt; ground broke May 2007 and it opened Sept 2008. The infobox says $54M; a 2007 headline said $50M. The rebuild holds the 50,000 sq ft, two-story R. Kirk Landon Football Fieldhouse (14,000 sq ft weight room, equipment room, athletic training) and 8,500 sq ft of locker rooms. FIU unveiled the fieldhouse at the Sept 2009 home opener, a year after the stands opened, so it was the last part of this rebuild. It is the football team's home.
The infobox lists a 2012 expansion that raised capacity from 18,000 to 20,000. No cost or details given.

project: Stadium improvements (Riccardo Silva gift: turf and video board)
note: A $3.76M donation paid for a new FieldTurf surface and video board, finished April 2017. Field and fan items only.

project: Florida Field south end zone double deck with football training and weight rooms
note: Closed in the south end zone with a double-decked grandstand. Modern training and weight room facilities for the football team were built beneath it. Football offices stayed under the west stands. Cost not found.

project: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium north end zone upper deck (Touchdown Terrace)
note: Upper deck and club deck over the north end zone; capacity over 85,000. Cost not found.

project: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium west side press box and luxury boxes
note: Press box expanded with club seats and luxury boxes. A UF page says $54M went into the stadium in 2003-04.
Privately funded $28M addition at the stadium's southwest corner (2007-08): offices, meeting space, museum. Football's main home until 2022.
$15M announced when construction began in January 2015. Opened in 2015 (one report says August).

project: James W. "Bill" Heavener Football Training Center
note: Stand-alone 142,000 sq ft building. Construction began June 2020; team moved in Aug 14, 2022. One report says $86M.

A 61,000 sq ft coeducational athletics center on the Boca Raton campus, officially opened April 2001. FAU says it was completed under its $8M projected cost, so the cost is the budget figure. Football used it from 2001 until its offices and weight room moved into the Schmidt Family Complex (2020-21). It still houses cross country, track, soccer, softball and volleyball.
New on-campus stadium; ground broke fall 2010, first game October 15, 2011. $70M is the projected and most-cited figure. The source says nothing about team spaces (locker room, offices).

project: Schmidt Family Complex for Academic and Athletic Excellence
note: A building of about 121,000 sq ft beside FAU Stadium, started with a $16M Schmidt Family Foundation gift (FAU's largest). Ground broke Jan 2017. Phase one holds the football offices, the football weight room, a sports medicine center and the department's academic support center. The ribbon cutting was Dec 2, 2021; FAU athletics also says it opened in 2020. Early estimates ran $40-65M; FAU athletics later gave $72M. The planned phase two indoor practice facility had no timetable, and no evidence was found that it was built.

project: Moore Athletic Center rebuild (University Center D)
note: Building D behind the north end zone replaced the 1950s Moore Athletic Center. It held football lockers, weight rooms, sports medicine and coaches' offices until the 2025 Dunlap Football Center. The infobox says done 2002, the text says the old building was razed 2002-03, and a booster piece says 2004; the opening year is uncertain. Cost not found.

project: Albert J. Dunlap Athletic Training Facility (indoor practice)
note: Ground broke Nov 2012 on the football practice fields and it was unveiled in 2013. Tomahawk Nation calls it a $15M project, with a $5M Dunlap lead gift.

project: Doak Campbell Stadium Champions Club and north end zone renovation
note: Champions Club, north end zone videoboard and sound system. Figures vary: about $50M for the club plus $15M for boards, $79.5M for the package (Tomahawk Nation and Football Stadium Digest), and more than $95M (WTXL). Athletic Business lists a narrower $34.5M scope.

project: Albert J. and Judith A. Dunlap Football Center
note: About 150,000 sq ft, football only. Ground broke Dec 17, 2022 and it opened Oct 2025. The estimate was about $100M at groundbreaking and $138M in the later board budget, which is the most cited figure. $20M Dunlap lead gift.

project: Doak Campbell Stadium renovation (west side rebuild, premium seating, seat widening)
note: The west side was rebuilt with Founders suites and clubs, south end zone premium seats added, and seats widened, cutting capacity to about 67,000. Work ran in phases over 2024-25 (temporary seating in 2024) and finished Aug 2025.
New on-campus stadium for 30,000. Ground broke June 1979 and it opened in 1980 for $7.198M. Team spaces not described.
Approved 1989 and finished 1991: 22 east side sky suites, 2,000 chair seats and 7,200 bench seats, with capacity going from 30,000 to about 40,000. No cost given.

project: Duncan Building expansion (football locker room, offices, meeting rooms)
note: An addition of more than 22,000 sq ft to the Duncan Building, football's home, bid together with the Ricchiuti Academic Center (Harris Construction). It added a new football locker room, coaching offices, team meeting rooms and a theater-style auditorium. Groundbreaking was Feb-Mar 2004, with completion expected Oct 2004. No separate cost found. The original Duncan Building came from a $1.3M drive led by booster Bob Duncan, but no date was found. A full Duncan renovation is planned in the Elevate campaign, with no start found.
Dedicated April 25, 1987. Athletics headquarters and football's operations hub. Another UGA release says more than $12M.

project: Sanford Stadium west end zone lower bowl enclosure
note: Added 4,205 seats; capacity 85,434.

project: Sanford Stadium south side luxury suites
note: 30 suites in 1994, raised to 50 in 2000. The $18M covers both projects together.

project: Sanford Stadium north side upper deck
note: Added 5,500 seats; capacity 92,058.
27 SkySuites; capacity 92,746.
Dedicated Feb 24, 2011. UGA called it a $33M, 53,000 sq ft upgrade to the football areas. Georgia's athletics site describes a $40M expansion and renovation.

project: William Porter Payne and Porter Otis Payne Indoor Athletic Facility
note: In use from January 2017, dedicated Feb 14, 2017. Fully privately funded. Groundbreaking ceremony in 2016 with Kirby Smart; one report says site work started about two months before it. Named in 2018.

project: Sanford Stadium west end zone renovation
note: Moved the home locker room from the east side to the west side and added a recruiting pavilion and plaza. Construction began after the 2017 season; ribbon cut Aug 31, 2018.

Approved Sept 2019; construction began January 2020. 165,000 sq ft of new and improved space: weight room, sports medicine, locker room, lounge. The first phase was ready for football after spring 2021; full dedication came later (year not confirmed).

project: Sanford Stadium south side renovation and new press box
note: Regents approved $68.5M in Aug 2022. 50 Yard Line Club, new southwest-corner press box, concourse work. Built in phases after the 2022 and 2023 seasons.
New stadium dedicated September 29, 1984, $4.7M. It came with the Lupton Building, the original fieldhouse (replaced in 2006). That this fieldhouse held team dressing rooms is inferred, not stated.

project: Gene Bishop Fieldhouse at Paulson Stadium
note: Replaced the Lupton Building in the west end. Field level has team and officials' dressing rooms; second level has hospitality and club seating. No cost found.

project: Paulson Stadium north stands expansion (FBS move)
note: About 6,300 seats on the north side; capacity to 25,000. Same project and groundbreak as the Ted Smith Center. Mid-deck finished spring 2014. No separate cost.

project: Ted Smith Family Football Center (Football Operations Center)
note: 57,000 sq ft in the east end of Paulson Stadium: coaches' offices, meeting rooms, locker rooms, rehab, weight room and the football Hall of Fame. Groundbreak June 2013, dedicated August 16, 2014. The infobox also lists $10M as the 2014 expansion cost.

project: Georgia State football practice facility (188 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive)
note: Groundbreak November 20, 2008. Existing buildings were turned into football facilities and offices, with a 100-yard turf field and a 50-yard grass field. The team was working out there by March 2010. No cost found.

project: Georgia State Stadium (now Center Parc Stadium), conversion of Turner Field
note: $52.8M was the expected cost for buying and renovating the stadium. Work started February 27, 2017; first game August 31, 2017; phase two built out the rest in 2018. Work included upgraded locker rooms, a turf field and a reoriented lower bowl.

project: Arthur B. Edge Jr. Intercollegiate Athletic Center
note: Athletics headquarters from 1982, with the football office on the second floor. It was demolished in 2024 for the Fanning Center (listed separately), so it is no longer standing even though the schema calls it open. A planned $70M renovation was dropped in favor of replacing it.

project: Bobby Dodd Stadium expansion and renovation
note: Two phases after the 2001 season: the north stands were rebuilt and bowled in for 2002, then a free-standing upper deck was added for 2003. The football locker room under the north stands was built in 2003 as part of it (AJC). Work started 'following the 2001 season'; the exact start date was not found.

project: John and Mary Brock Indoor Practice Facility
note: About 88,000 sq ft. Ground broke Jan 2011 and it opened Aug 2011. Costs conflict: the 2010 estimate was $6-7M, the AJC says $7M, and a Georgia Tech-linked page says about $9M. The Brocks gave $3.5M.

project: Football locker room renovation (Bobby Dodd Stadium)
note: 8,100 sq ft room under the north stands, the first renovation since 2003. Work began Jan 2018 and the room was shown to the team July 25, 2018. Paid for by an anonymous donor.

project: Thomas A. Fanning Student-Athlete Performance Center
note: Over 100,000 sq ft, built at Bobby Dodd Stadium in place of the Edge/Rice buildings, with meeting and office space for football only. Ground broke March 25, 2024 and it opened May 2026. An earlier report said $85M.
State-owned stadium, Hawaii's home from 1975. It stopped hosting fan events Dec 17, 2020 and has been demolished since Feb 2026, so it no longer stands. Cost $37M. Team spaces not described.

project: Clarence T. C. Ching Athletics Complex (practice field and building)
note: Opened 2015, two years late. It normally serves as the football team's practice facility. Its three-story building has locker rooms for beach volleyball, cross country, soccer and track, not football. Estimated at $10M and ran 60% over budget (about $16M implied, not stated as a figure).

project: Ching Complex conversion for home football games
note: After Aloha Stadium closed, it was readied for 2021 home games: about 9,000 seats, new turf, scoreboard and speakers, and an upgraded press box. No cost given.

project: Ching Complex expansion to about 15,000 seats
note: Regents approved a two-phase, $30M expansion in Aug 2022: a bigger mauka sideline stand with hospitality areas, end zone stands, filled corners, and the old Aloha Stadium video board. Capacity is 15,194 from 2023. Seating and hospitality only.

A $3.3M renovation over the year before Feb 2024 of the department's weight room in the arena (the facility dates to 1994). It added 24 power racks with tracking and a nutrition station, and serves about 500 athletes in 21 sports, football included. During the work, football trained in Klum Gym's 'Iron Church'.

Field lowered nine feet, track removed, sideline and end zone seats and 20 suites added; John O'Quinn gave the lead gift. UH moved all home games back from the Astrodome in 1998 at 32,000 seats, but the article dates the heavy renovation to 1999. Demolished in 2012. No cost found.

New stadium on the Robertson site, groundbreaking Feb 8, 2013, opened Aug 29, 2014. It includes the team's locker room next to the field-level club. A 2014 student paper reported it ran $16M over budget.

project: Indoor Practice Facility (next to TDECU Stadium)
note: Full-size indoor turf field with space set aside for a future football-only weight room. Regents approved it Aug 25, 2016. Construction began after the 2016 season (late 2016 or early 2017) and finished fall 2017.

A football-only operations center beside TDECU Stadium: locker room, a 21,000 sq ft second-floor weight room, recovery, meeting rooms and offices. UH gives a $130M construction cost; earlier coverage said $140M and one outlet $160M. Ceremonial groundbreaking Nov 2023; the team moved in late July 2025, with the ribbon cutting Aug 27, 2025.
Inflated over the stadium field each winter from December 1985 to spring 2000. Replaced by the Irwin facility, so no longer standing.

project: Memorial Stadium renovation with new football headquarters
note: $7M renovation began April 1985: new AstroTurf and a new football headquarters in the stadium's northeast corner. The finish year is not stated; 1985 assumed.

project: Memorial Stadium upper-deck and bleacher renovation
note: Ran November 1991 to August 1992. Replaced the upper-deck concrete bleachers and upgraded restrooms, electrical and drainage. No team spaces.
Replaced The Bubble; Wikipedia says 2001, another source says 2000. No cost found. Still in use; the Smith Center is attached to it.

Approved at $116M (2006); later reports put the final cost at $120-121M. Work began after the 2006 season; rededicated September 2008. Added concourses, a north end-zone stand and west-side suites and press box.

project: Henry Dale and Betty Smith Football Center
note: 107,650 sq ft, $79.2M; players moved in August 2019. A June 2017 AP report said ground would break the next year; construction reportedly started January 2018. No ceremony date found.
$6.5M, 96,129 sq ft indoor field, dedicated April 1996, with two outdoor grass fields beside it. Turf replaced 2024, plus later upgrades of about $3M (year and scope unclear).

project: North End Zone Student-Athlete Development Center (Memorial Stadium)
note: Enclosed the north end zone with a 25,000 sq ft weight/training room, classrooms and Henke Hall of Champions; old bleachers demolished January 2007. The $55M is an umbrella figure that covered several IU facility projects, not this building alone.

project: South End Zone enclosure / Excellence Academy (Memorial Stadium)
note: $53M most cited ($48M for the building alone in a dedication release). Holds rehab and treatment space for all IU athletes plus academic space, so it is not football-only team space. Groundbreaking April 28, 2017.
$8.5M expanded and renovated locker room, training room and players' lounge, built in about six months.
Air-supported dome built for about $2.7M (figure from one source). Collapsed under snow in December 1990 and was re-erected. Deflated April 2012 and replaced by the 2012 indoor facility.

Regents approved $86.8M in March 2004 (about $90M often quoted). Phase I started right after the 2004 season. New locker rooms, training room and press box; the south end-zone part with the locker rooms was done before the 2005 season, and the whole project in 2006.

project: Indoor practice facility (football performance center phase I)
note: About 102,000 sq ft, opened August 2012; phase I also reconfigured the Kenyon outdoor fields. Budgeted at about $20M and reported under budget; it was phase one of a $55M two-phase project. Later named for the Hansens.

project: Stew and LeNore Hansen Football Performance Center (Jacobson football operations building, phase II)
note: Phase II was budgeted at $35M; Athletic Business lists construction at $43.7M and occupancy December 2014, with finishing touches in 2015. Holds locker rooms, the weight room, training rooms and offices.

project: Kinnick Stadium north end zone renovation
note: Approved 2016 and finished before the 2019 season. Box and club seating plus a new scoreboard; no team spaces.
New stadium; groundbreaking Oct 26, 1973, first game Sept 20, 1975, with 42,500 seats. The sources do not say whether it had team rooms.

project: Richard O. Jacobson Athletic Building (with Olsen Building renovation)
note: Athletics building in the north end zone, built 1995-96 (the sources give 1995 and 1996). With the renovated Olsen Building, it held football's offices, locker room, meeting rooms, weight room and sports medicine until the 2012 Bergstrom complex.

project: Jack Trice Stadium west side press tower
note: Three-level press tower with nine sky box suites.
92,000 sq ft indoor building with a full football field, opened March 2004, privately funded. Also used by softball and soccer.
22 new suites, wider concourses, a club section and a plaza, done between the 2007 and 2009 seasons. Fan amenities only.

156,000 sq ft expansion between the indoor facility and the Jacobson Building: weight room, coaches' offices, position meeting rooms, auditorium, locker rooms and a new indoor turf. Dedicated Oct 26, 2012.

project: Jack Trice Stadium south end zone enclosure
note: Enclosed the south end zone with an upper deck and a 40,000 sq ft premium club; capacity rose to 61,500. Estimated at $60M (Reiman family gave $25M). Regents approved it Feb 6, 2014, and it opened for the 2015 season. The 2014 groundbreaking year is my inference from that timeline.
100,000 sq ft building northwest of the stadium with a new football locker room and study and nutrition areas. The Olsen Building was demolished for a plaza, and the concourse loop was finished.
Wikipedia says only that a field house was built at the stadium in 1977. Its contents, its cost and whether football still uses it are unknown.

project: Burgess-Snow Field expansion and Stadium Tower (Meehan Hall)
note: Added seats in the south stands and east end zone (24,000 capacity) and a seven-story tower: a residence hall on floors 1-4, skyboxes and press box on 5-7. The infobox gives $47M. Rededicated Sept 11, 2010. No team spaces mentioned.

project: Loring and Debbie White Football Complex
note: A 52,000 sq ft football operations building behind the west end zone of AmFirst Stadium, costing $32.8M. It has a new locker room ('The Daug House'), training room, equipment room and coaches' offices. Ground broke April 2023 and it opened for the 2024 season. The planned $23M Ken and Jenny Howell indoor practice facility (with an 11,424 sq ft football weight room) was only approved and named in Feb 2026, with no groundbreaking by 2025, so it is left out.
Multi-purpose stadium with about 5,200 seats. It held athletics administrative offices, classrooms and racquetball courts; no football team spaces are described.

project: Robert & Frances Plecker Athletic Performance Center
note: A two-story building beside Bridgeforth that holds nearly every part of the football program (offices, locker room, weight room). Announced fall 2001; construction began August 2002; opened spring semester 2005. JMU Athletics gives $10M, a 2003 Board of Visitors summary $9.8M and Athletic Business $8.46M construction cost. The weight room was overhauled in 2022 (Moats Family S&C Facility: flooring and equipment, cost not found).

Began December 2009, done August 2011. Two-tier west complex with an upper deck, 17 suites, club lounge and video board; capacity 24,877. The whole stadium complex, including the Plecker Athletic Performance Center and parking deck, is about $90M.

A 182 by 180 ft fabric ClearSpan building used as JMU football's indoor field, from the supplier's post of April 29, 2019. The opening year is taken from that post (it may be 2018 or 2019). Cost not found. It is a modest tension-fabric structure, not a full-length indoor field.

project: Memorial Stadium 1998-99 renovation, press box and suites
note: 1998 infrastructure renovation (lights in 1997), then the press box and scholarship suites expanded in 1999 with a video board. No cost found.
Offices, weight room, locker rooms, meeting rooms, hydrotherapy and nutrition area, with new practice fields southeast of the stadium. Broke ground Oct 6, 2006, and officially opened July 30, 2008.
New seats, a touchdown club behind the north end zone and new exterior banners. Fan side only. No cost found.
Next to the west side of the stadium, built only with private gifts (notably David Booth). The $26M and Feb 2019 opening come from KU's facility page as shown in a search result.

project: David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium rebuild (Gateway District), phase 1
note: Near-total demolition began after the 2023 season; KU played 2024 in Kansas City. Phase 1 (new west stands and a north end conference center) was ready for 2025. Phase 2 (east stands) is due in 2027 at 43,000 seats. Booth pledged $50M in 2017. Total cost and any team rooms are not in the source.
Team home on the north end of the stadium from 1988, replaced by the new Vanier complex in 2015. Cost unknown.

project: Dev Nelson press box and suites
note: Five-level press box and suites on the west side, built for the stadium's 25th anniversary. Imploded Dec 2012 for the West Side Stadium Center.

project: East side upper deck, club seats and suites
note: Built after the 1998 season (HOK Sport design); capacity rose to 50,300.

project: Locker room complex renovation and north end zone seats
note: Renovated locker room complex with a new hydrotherapy center, about 1,900 north end zone seats and new electronics, before the 2006 season. The $5.6M covers all of it.

About 250,000 sq ft: press box, suites, club and loge seats, concourses, Hall of Honor and a student-athlete dining hall. No football locker, weight or office space. Broke ground before the 2012 spring game; dedicated Aug 30, 2013.

North end zone rebuild finished Aug 2015: 1,800 sq ft locker room, 10,000 sq ft weight room, training and recovery, coaches' offices, player lounge, team entrance and seats. Also holds athletics administration and the student-athlete center.
South end zone structure joined to Bramlage Coliseum: 13,500 sq ft club, loges, suites and concourse. Began Feb 2019 and was unveiled Sept 2021. Premium seating only.

project: Indoor Football Practice Facility (next to the stadium)
note: Indoor and outdoor practice fields with direct access to the stadium and Vanier, plus east concourse work. Broke ground Dec 8, 2021, on a $32.5M budget, set to open Oct 2022; the actual opening date is not confirmed. It replaces the old indoor complex south of Bramlage Coliseum, which becomes indoor track.

Built as a soccer-specific stadium in a public-private partnership with the Atlanta Beat; opened May 2, 2010, cost $16.5M. Football has played there since 2015. A 2016 plan to expand it was still unfunded in 2018.

project: Football offices and weight room, Town Point Drive
note: Football offices opened October 2013 in an office building at 3380 Town Point Drive: 29,500 sq ft with 16 offices and a 6,860 sq ft weight and agility area. A build-out of existing office space, cost not found. Still the football home until the Wellstar Champions Complex (a renovated 78,000 sq ft former office building, about $11.75M-$13.2M, move-in fall 2027) is done. That project is left out because no groundbreaking by 2025 was found.

Opened 1990: full-size football field, six-lane track, a weight room (named for James Harrison) and locker rooms. Used mainly by football. The 2014 expansion added locker rooms for other sports only. Cost not found.
East bleachers condemned and torn down in 2001; new student bleacher section ready for 2003. Seating only.

Phase 1 (2007): press box canopy, gates, ticket office. Phase 2 (2008): south end zone seats torn down, HD scoreboard, concessions, plaza. No team spaces. A plan from the 2013 'Building Champions' campaign for a coaches' office building and locker room upgrades was never built.
Football training facility built in 1987. Football's home until the Joe Craft facility opened next door in 2016. Cost not found.
Indoor practice facility shared with track; its football field was short of regulation size. Sources say it was built in 1992 or 1993.

project: Commonwealth Stadium end zone enclosures and suites
note: Enclosed both end zones and added 40 suites; capacity 67,530.
New press box, premium seats, concourses, facade and a recruiting room; capacity cut to about 61,000. Locker room work not confirmed, so team_spaces is false.
100,000 sq ft. Trustees approved it in Jan 2014. It opened July 2016 after 19 months of construction, which puts the start around late 2014.

project: Nutter Field House renovation (full-length football field)
note: $5M share of a $30M package approved in 2022. Track moved out and replaced with a 120-yard football-only turf field. Work ran spring to summer 2023.
83,580 sq ft, climate-controlled, connected to the Football Operations Center. Cost not found.
11,600 seats including 70 suites; capacity 91,600. WBRZ gives $50M.
All-in-one building: locker room, weight room, training room, video center, coaches' offices.

project: Tiger Stadium west upper deck rebuild (Stadium Club)
note: Old west upper deck torn down at the end of 2004; new suites, club seats and press box. Hurricane Katrina pushed completion from 2005 to 2006.

project: Tiger Stadium south end zone upper deck
note: Approved April 2012; construction from Oct 17, 2012 to summer 2014. 70 suites and 3,000 club seats; capacity 102,321.

project: Football Operations Center renovation and expansion
note: Unveiled July 2019. Nearly 25,000 sq ft added: new locker room with sleep pods, training room, offices, players' lounge and nutrition center. Privately funded.

Ground broke May 8, 1989; opened Oct 21, 1989. The football program moved its operations there in 1989. The infobox gives $18M, but that matches the 2010 phase-one estimate exactly, so the original cost may be mixed up.

project: Williams Stadium expansion phase one (press tower and 7,200 seats)
note: Announced Aug 2009: five-story press tower with 18 suites and a second deck on the home side (19,200 seats). Estimated $18M; the tower was ready Oct 2, 2010. The infobox lists renovation as 2010-2011.
Indoor practice facility opened in 2017 at a cost of $29M.

project: Williams Stadium expansion phase two (student-side upper deck)
note: Second deck on the student side raised capacity to 25,000 for the 2018 season. Estimated $40M. The groundbreaking year comes from the infobox's 2017-2018 renovation dates.
Finished April 2020 at the north end of Williams Stadium: home locker room, coaches' offices, meeting rooms, training room and a 16,000 sq ft weight room. Cost not found.
Built in 1970 to replace McNaspy Stadium; opened September 25, 1971. Players enter through a tunnel from the athletics complex. No cost or team-space details.
Capacity from 26,000 to 31,000 through added end seating. Seating only.
Finished August 2007 for about $4.5M. Full 120-yard turf field, plus a basketball practice court and batting cages that other sports share.

project: Cajun Field south end zone seating (athletics master plan phase one)
note: Started spring 2014, done for the 2014 season: bowled south end zone with bleachers, concessions and restrooms, and a new north end zone video board. Not team spaces.

project: Donald and Janice Mosing Student-Athlete Performance Center
note: 100,000 sq ft, opened September 2015. Football offices, a 12,000 sq ft weight room, athletic training and hydrotherapy, nutrition station, equipment room and a 150-seat auditorium. No cost found.

project: Cajun Field at Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium renovation (new west tower)
note: $75M announced in June 2021. Work began after the 2023 season and finished before 2025. The west tower was replaced with suites, club seats, loge boxes and a press box; no team spaces mentioned. Capacity now 30,392.
Capacity raised to 30,600. The sky box was added in 1985 per the program article (the stadium article says it was expanded in 1988). Seating and press areas only.
15,000 sq ft at the south end zone, opened June 2001. Coaches' offices, team meeting rooms, the Bundrick Sports Medicine Center and a football museum. Privately funded.

Three stories and 70,000 sq ft behind the south end zone, opened September 4, 2015. Weight room, locker room, players' lounge, auditorium, coaches' offices, position meeting rooms and a club level. Under construction in 2014; exact groundbreak year not found.

project: Joe Aillet Stadium press box and sky box replacement
note: Home-side sky box renovated and replaced for 2017, with luxury suites and coaches', media and officials' areas. Premium and press only.

project: Cardinal Stadium (now L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium)
note: New 42,000-seat on-campus stadium. Ground broke June 19, 1996. The program article says $63M; the stadium infobox says $135M. The football complex in the north end was built with it and is listed as its own row.

Two stories, about 68,445 sq ft, at the stadium's north end. Holds coaches' offices, weight room, training room, equipment and academic services. Dates to 1998 and named in 2006. Its own cost is not found because it was built with the stadium.

120-yard FieldTurf field. Construction began late May 2005 and the first practice was Dec 1, 2005. The school's releases say $8M ($2M Trager lead gift). Wikipedia says $10M and 2006, and another page says 2019; the 2005 school releases are preferred.

project: Papa John's Cardinal Stadium expansion (east side upper deck, south terrace)
note: About 13,000 seats including 1,725 club seats, 33 suites and the PNC Club. Construction started Dec 1, 2008 and finished for the 2010 season. About 46% state-funded.

project: North end zone enclosure and Schnellenberger Complex expansion
note: One $63M project: the north end zone was enclosed (about 5,400-6,000 seats, suites, club seats) and the football complex expanded (weight room, team meeting rooms, hydrotherapy, lounges, offices). Work began after the last home game of 2016 and was first used Sept 8, 2018. Announced in 2015 at $55M. Wikipedia says completed 2019.

project: Marshall University Stadium (now Joan C. Edwards Stadium) with the Shewey Athletic Center
note: New $30M stadium; groundbreak July 18, 1990, opened September 7, 1991. Its north end Shewey Athletic Center holds the locker rooms and football and athletics offices. That part was unfinished in 1991; staff moved in July 1992.

project: Joan C. Edwards Stadium seating expansion
note: Seating to 38,019 before the 2000 opener; 2,000 seats were also added in 1994. Seating only.

project: Chris Cline Athletic Complex (indoor practice facility)
note: Part of the Herd Vision campaign announced in 2012, on the old Sam Hood Field site; opened September 2014. Indoor football practice field, indoor track, Hall of Fame and the Marshall Sports Medicine Institute. Groundbreak year not found.
$7M team house beside the east end zone with the locker room, offices and medical areas. One source says 1992. Football moved to Jones-Hill House in 2021.

project: Tyser Tower (Byrd Stadium suites and press area)
note: Five-story south-side tower with luxury suites and an expanded press area. No cost found; rebuilt in 2007-09.
12,000-seat north upper deck raised capacity to 48,055. No cost found.

project: Gossett Football Team House expansion and remodel
note: Expansion started 2002; the remodel (meeting rooms, dining, auditorium) was done summer 2004. About 19,000 sq ft added and 45,000 sq ft renovated. No cost found.
Ran 2007-2009. Rebuilt Tyser Tower with 63 suites and mezzanine seating and lowered the field. No team spaces.

project: Jones-Hill House football performance center (Cole Field House phase II)
note: Football's home inside the converted Cole Field House: a 100-yard indoor field (phase I, opened August 2017) plus the phase II operations center (weight rooms, locker room, offices), begun late 2017 and opened June 4, 2021. Athletics put the football project at $149.3M (planned at $155M); this row covers both phases. Wikipedia's $196M is the whole building, including the separate academic Center for Sports Medicine, Health and Human Performance and an incubator.

The football team's home on the Park Avenue campus (offices, locker room, football weight room), also holding the Olympic sports weight room. A search summary of the athletics pages gives a 1970 opening, which I couldn't confirm. Cost not found. Later expanded with the 2019 to 2020 addition and indoor facility (own row).

project: Liberty Bowl Memorial Stadium 1987 renovation and expansion
note: The infobox lists $19.5M for the 1987 renovations (expanded 1987). Elsewhere the article describes a $12M facelift that raised the east stands (about 12,000 seats) and added a suite level to lure an NFL team; this is likely the same work, but the figures conflict.

A football-only weight room of about 13,000 sq ft in the Murphy Complex, opened February 2011, with a 30-yard turf area, later rebranded and re-equipped. Cost not found, so it may fall below $3M. Separately, the locker room was remade in fall 2011 with a gift from DeAngelo Williams (cost not found).

project: Liberty Bowl stadium improvements and Tiger Lane
note: 2013 facelift: paint, lighting, elevators, turf, renovated luxury boxes, accessibility work, video boards, and the 17-acre Tiger Lane green space. No team spaces mentioned.

project: Indoor practice facility (Hardin Family Field) and Murphy Complex addition
note: Two phases, $11.2M final ($10.6M estimate plus $0.6M of gifts for design). Phase I was a 25,000 sq ft addition to the Murphy Complex with a training room, dining and offices, opened summer 2019. Phase II was the full-length indoor field (74,000-78,000 sq ft), ribbon-cut June 17, 2020. Trustees approved $10M of bond financing in August 2017; groundbreak 2017 is from Athletic Business's 'Work Begins on Memphis Indoor Practice Facility' (https://www.athleticbusiness.com/facilities/fitness/news/15150131/work-begins-on-memphis-indoor-practice-facility), and the field phase began in 2019.

project: Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium renovation (west side rebuild)
note: Announced 2022 at about $200M. Funding of $220M was set in January 2024 ($120M city, $50M Fred Smith, $50M university). It replaces the west tower and most of the west bowl and renovates the east suites and hospitality spaces. Construction began after the 2023 season and was planned to finish before the 2025 season; actual completion is not confirmed. No team spaces mentioned.

project: Isadore Hecht Athletic Center (expansion and dedication)
note: Built 1951, then expanded, renovated and named for Isadore Hecht in 1979. Football's training facility and offices, plus the athletics administration. A later expansion (reported as $8M in 2001) and a 2015 makeover could not be pinned to a source, so they are not listed.
Attached to the Hecht Center and dedicated Oct 4, 2013. A new football locker room, sports medicine and training area, and academic center. The 2010 projection was $13.6M; about $15M is also cited.

Miami's home field since 2008, owned by the Dolphins. A privately funded $350M (Wikipedia figure) renovation with a canopy and amenities began Jan 2015 and was done for 2016. Not a Miami project and not team space.

Over 100,000 sq ft with two turf fields and a mezzanine of football coaches' offices and meeting rooms. Ground broke May 2017; the first practice was Aug 2018. Most reports say $34M ($14M Soffer gift); the athletics site now says $40M, and the fundraising goal rose to $40M.
New stadium replacing Miami Field, $13.5M, opened Oct 1, 1983. It holds the football offices, player meeting rooms and locker rooms, so team_spaces true.

project: Yager Stadium upgrades (FieldTurf, lights, video boards, bleachers)
note: A series of upgrades: FieldTurf 2003; permanent lights, scoreboard with three video boards and the Cradle of Coaches plaza 2004; new student bleachers 2005. Cost not found.
91,000 sq ft at the north end zone, with a turf football field (Roethlisberger field) and track practice areas. $14M from the cited Journal-News headline (April 2015). Groundbreaking year not found.
Built 1980; football's main indoor practice site until Glick Field House opened in 2009. No original cost found.
Football building completed in 1990: locker rooms, meeting rooms, medical and training areas. A September 24, 1990 Michigan Daily article gives 64,000 sq ft at $12M, all funded by alumni.
About 104,000 sq ft, $26.1M; occupied August 7, 2009.
Approved June 2007; work was under way by 2008 and the stadium was rededicated in 2010. Press box, 83 suites and 3,200 club seats; no team-space work found.

project: Schembechler Hall entrance, museum and recruiting space renovation
note: Approved 2012. Added about 7,000 sq ft (museum, exhibit, office and recruiting spaces); completed April 2014.

project: Football performance center (weight room) inside Oosterbaan Field House
note: Approved February 2017; adds a 32,000 sq ft football weight room plus a roof replacement. Completed January 2018.

project: Schembechler Hall football performance center (athletic medicine, rehab and nutrition)
note: Approved May 2017: renovates about 24,000 sq ft and adds 8,000 sq ft. One source gives a May 2019 grand opening; another names a September ribbon-cutting with no year.

project: Schembechler Hall football locker room renovation
note: Approved October 2023 at an estimated $14M and unveiled before the 2024 season. First locker room expansion since 2009; a $6M gift adds a players' lounge and barbershop.
Built 1980 for $1.75M (per a search-result summary). The complex holds an 86,000 sq ft indoor practice field, but the field's build date (likely 1980s) and cost are not confirmed.
Eight-story addition under construction from 2003, unveiled September 2005. Suites, club seats, press box, a recruiting lounge and university offices; no locker or weight rooms.

project: Skandalaris Football Center (Duffy Daugherty Building expansion)
note: 25,000 sq ft addition (team and position meeting rooms, coaches' offices, players' lounge), dedicated August 21, 2008. Reported as a $15M project or $15.5M. A separate $2M weight room expansion in 2008 is below the threshold.

project: Spartan Stadium North End Zone Complex
note: 50,000 sq ft addition with a new home locker room (Rachel Fairman Adams Spartan Locker Room) and home training room. Planned at $18-20M; dedicated at $24.5M in August 2014.

Addition to and renovation of the Duffy/Skandalaris buildings. MSU's figure is $67.75M (some outlets say about $78M). Construction began April 2022; the team moved into the locker room August 2023; dedicated April 2024.

project: Spartan Stadium video board and West Tower premium renovation
note: Approved December 2024: $10M for video boards and $18M for premium floors, scheduled to finish August 2025. No team spaces.

project: Floyd Stadium renovation (west side, press tower, club level)
note: $25M renovation for the move to I-A. Ground broke Jan 1997; first game Sept 5, 1998; 30,788 seats, a five-story press and suite tower, club level. The article lists team meeting rooms and a 10,000 sq ft all-sport weight room in the stadium complex but doesn't date them to this project.

project: Stephen and Denise Smith Student-Athlete Performance Center
note: 85,000 sq ft, three-story building in Floyd Stadium's north end zone: home of MTSU football and a performance and recovery hub for all 17 teams (weight room, training room, equipment rooms, football offices and meeting rooms). $66M; ground broke Jan 2023; ribbon cut July 30, 2025.
Built 1985 for $5.5M with the indoor practice field (55-ft ceiling), offices, locker room, meeting rooms and training room. Later renovated (one report says about $1M, date unclear).

project: TCF Bank Stadium (now Huntington Bank Stadium)
note: New on-campus stadium, groundbreaking September 30, 2006. Built the Murray Warmath home locker room, training and therapy rooms. Total $303.4M (stadium construction figure $288.5M).

project: Athletes Village indoor football practice facility
note: 85-ft-tall indoor field, part of the $166M Athletes Village (cost in the row above). A March 2025 report still says the team practices in Gibson-Nagurski.

The $166M covers the whole multi-sport Athletes Village: the Larson Football Performance Center, the indoor football practice building, basketball facilities, and academic, nutrition and sports medicine space. No football-only figure was found. Ceremonial groundbreaking October 30, 2015; occupancy January 2018.
Added almost 9,000 seats. Raised without state money.

project: Davis Wade Stadium expansion and renovation
note: Started 1999, done 2002: 50 skyboxes, club seats, second upper deck; capacity 55,082. Figures conflict: the article text says $50M, its infobox says $21M. Turman Fieldhouse locker rooms were remodeled in 1999 (cost not found).

Indoor facility shared with baseball; football field is about 50 yards. Ground broke Nov 2004; finished around early 2006. Another report gives $3M. A football-only indoor facility ($60M) is set to break ground in 2027, so it is not listed.
80,000 sq ft; officially opened January 2013. The groundbreaking photo is on a 2011 university page. Early estimate was $20-25M including practice field work.

project: Davis Wade Stadium north end zone expansion
note: Closed in the north end zone and added a new west concourse; capacity 61,337. Finished August 2014.
Indoor facility with only a 70-yard field. Replaced as football's indoor by the Stephens Indoor Facility in 2023.

project: Memorial Stadium press box and suite tower
note: Started before the 1999 season, finished August 2000. Press, coaches' boxes, suites and club seats.

project: Mizzou Athletics Training Complex renovation and expansion
note: Over 101,000 sq ft, with a 15,000 sq ft weight room and the football locker room. Football's home from the 1980s to 2019. Opening is July 2008 per Mizzou, Feb 2007 per Athletic Business.

project: Memorial Stadium east side upper balcony and press box conversion
note: Press box converted to suites in 2013; east upper balcony (5,200 seats plus 800 club) in 2014. The planned $72M was for the whole SEC-entry expansion.

New home for the football program: both teams' locker rooms, football weight room, meeting rooms, medical, nutrition and staff offices, plus suites and clubs. Approved at $89M late in 2017; reported at $98M on opening.
86,400 sq ft with a full-length field. Ground broke Nov 2021; first used July 31, 2023. Approved at $33.1M, privately funded.

project: Memorial Stadium north end zone (Centennial project)
note: Final approval Sept 12, 2024; work set to start Nov 30, 2024 and finish for the 2026 season. Premium seating, Rock M Club, concourses. Capacity 63,609 listed for 2026.

project: Plaster Sports Complex renovation (upper deck, suites, press box)
note: Robert Plaster's gift paid for an 8,500-seat upper deck, 24 suites, a press box, a track and turf. The complex has an athletics strength and conditioning center on its second level, but Wikipedia doesn't say it was built in 1991. Cost not found.

project: Plaster Stadium east side rebuild and track removal
note: Old east student bleachers torn down after the 2013 season and rebuilt (paid by the B.E.A.R. student fee). The track was removed and the field moved, making it football-only; 17,500 seats. The Plaster part of a roughly $22M athletics and recreation package also renovated team facilities, with seating, concessions, restrooms and ticket windows. That $22M covers several projects, so this row's cost stays unknown. The team's offices and locker rooms were not built in this project.

project: Wendell H. Murphy Football Center and south end zone enclosure
note: Football operations center behind the south end zone, spanning the field's width (about 103,000 sq ft). Built as phase two of a four-phase Carter-Finley renovation that began before the 2001 season, and dedicated and ribbon-cut April 25, 2003 (one Wolfpacker piece says it opened in 2002). Paid for by the Student Aid Association. Cost not found.
Luxury boxes, club seats and media facilities, built after the 2004 season and opened for 2005. Cost not found.

project: Carter-Finley Stadium north end zone grandstand
note: 5,730 chairback, bench and accessible seats plus 1,630 bleachers, making the stadium a bowl (57,583). Also a north plaza and corner video screens. Cost not found.

A 92,000-93,000 sq ft building with a full 120-yard field, opened spring or summer 2015. Also used by track, soccer and baseball. The Wolfpack Club gives a $17.2M project; a UNC media piece and an engineering firm give $14M. Under construction through 2014 (gopack construction updates Feb and Sept 2014); the start date was not confirmed. Called Close-King, not Close-Moreno.

project: Murphy Center football locker room renovation
note: The football locker room in the Murphy Center was renovated after the 2015 season and opened July 2016. Cost not found, so it may fall below $3M. A 2023 weight room refurbishment (Fulford Family Weight Room, equipment and layout) is left out because no cost was found and it looks small.

2004: west side press box expansion. From 2005 on, ongoing work lowered the field, and added club seats and lounges, suites, end zone seating and banquet space, plus 'renovated locker room facilities'.
