That later work has no dates or costs, so this row only covers 2004 and is marked team_spaces false.

Ricketts Hall (built 1966, renovated 2004) holds the varsity football locker room, football offices, and the 12,000 sq ft Jack Lengyel Sports Conditioning Facility (weight room shared with lacrosse, baseball and wrestling). The renovation cost was not found, so it may not meet the $3M bar.

Ground broke March 25, 2006. The infobox gives $50.0M; a cited news headline says $52M. It has a full-length 76,000 sq ft retractable AstroTurf football field over a 200m track. Its weight room serves other sports, not football.
New press box and west facade; no team spaces found.
Full-length indoor field. The field house part was used in fall 2005; it opened to football in spring practice 2006. Its cost is inside the $50M North Stadium project. Revamped later (cost unknown).
cost_in: North Stadium expansion with Tom and Nancy Osborne Athletic Complex

project: North Stadium expansion with Tom and Nancy Osborne Athletic Complex
note: Osborne Complex: locker room, strength and conditioning, and offices; the north end zone also got 6,000+ seats. The $50M is the whole North Stadium project including the Hawks Center (Phase I was announced at $40M). Ground broke 2004.
6,000+ seats plus two 20,000 sq ft research facilities (one athletics research). No locker or weight rooms.

315,000 sq ft; announced at $155M, $165M at completion. Groundbreaking April 30, 2021. A report says the locker room and training areas were ready in fall (likely 2023) and the weight room opened March 2024; some sources say 2023.
Expanded 1990-1992, with capacity going from 14,000 to 31,545 in 1992. The infobox gives $6.5M for all the earlier expansions together (1978 and 1990-92), so no figure for this project alone.

The football program's 'command center' beside Mackay Stadium (locker room, coaches' offices, weight room). It began as a locker room building and had major renovations in 1989, 1993 and 2023. The original build year was not found, so 1993, its last major rebuild before 2023, is used. No costs found.
Regents approved an $11.5M bond in Dec 2014 for better seating, done for the 2016 season. Capacity fell to 26,000. Premium seating only.

project: Cashell Fieldhouse football locker room expansion
note: An expanded, donor-funded football locker room in Cashell, about $3M (bid range $2.95M-$3.15M), done for the 2023 season. It was part of a roughly $5M offseason package with new coaches' offices, the playing surface and the Bitonio Family Strength & Conditioning Center (about $1M). A later roundup gives $5.3M for the whole Cashell locker room job, which added women's team locker rooms.

project: University of Nevada Fieldhouse (indoor practice facility)
note: Regents approved it June 13, 2025, with ground broken August 19, 2025 (dirt moving by mid-September), topping out April 20, 2026, and the opening on October 20, 2026. It has 110 yards of indoor turf (a roughly 70-yard field plus end zones) and is multi-use. The $28M is the fieldhouse (https://nevadasportsnet.com/news/reporters/a-beacon-of-hope-nevada-athletics-places-final-beam-of-28-million-fieldhouse-project); the $32M figure adds two turf fields resurfaced. It is mostly paid for by a student fee. Football was due to start practicing inside in late November 2026.

A field house and athletic training facility built in 1995 just past the stadium's south end zone. A planned tunnel from the stadium to it is meant for player access to the locker rooms, so the team's locker rooms are there. No cost found.

project: University Stadium 2001 north end zone expansion
note: North end zone stands, restrooms, concessions and the LoboVision video board. No cost given.

project: New Mexico Mutual Champions Training Center
note: A multi-sport training center just outside the south end zone, joined to the Tow Diehm Facility. Planned in 2021 at $3.4M (with a $1M lead gift) and opened April 2023. Used by football and other teams, but football's own weight room stays in Tow Diehm, so it is not the team's main weight room.

project: Tow Diehm Facility expansion (team room and Paulsen strength center)
note: A $7.5M expansion of the football building: a dedicated team room or auditorium between the locker room and the weight room, the Mark Paulsen Strength & Conditioning Center expanded to 4,876 sq ft, a nutrition and fueling area and equipment space. The equipment phase was done before the 2025 season, so work began by 2025, but the exact start date was not found. Completion was announced June 2026. Earlier work below $3M: a 2014 weight room refurbishment (about $0.8M) and a 2018 locker room upgrade ($676,500).
Replaced the old Memorial Stadium. Ground broke March 1977, built in 18 months for $4M, first game Sept 16, 1978. The north end holds the locker rooms; assumed to be from the original build.
$6M building behind the south end zone (2004): athletics offices, an athletic training and education center, and club and skybox space. How much football uses it isn't spelled out.

project: Team meeting and video room complex (north end field house)
note: New team meeting and video rooms added next to the field house at the north end in 2007, the same year as a $1.5M scoreboard. Cost not found, so it may be under the $3M bar.

project: Kenan Stadium 1987-88 project (press box replaced, lights, lounges)
note: The old press box was replaced by 2,000 seats (capacity 52,000), with permanent lights, a chancellor's lounge and a lettermen's lounge. Wikipedia gives $7M but flags it citation needed.

project: Kenan Stadium 1995-98 renovation with the Frank H. Kenan Football Center
note: A new playing field, a new football building (Kenan Football Center) replacing cramped locker rooms, and 8,000 west end zone seats (6,000 in 1997, the rest in 1998, capacity 60,000). The football center's exact opening year and the cost were not found.

project: Kenan Football Center Phase I renovation (fifth floor, remodeled team spaces)
note: Added a fifth floor (about 15,000-17,000 sq ft) for recruiting and media and remodeled the offices and team spaces; done August 2009. Trustees approved $50M on July 23, 2008 for a larger concept (fifth and sixth floors with suites and premium seats), but zoning, insurance and cost issues cut it to one floor, so the $50M is not the final cost. No final figure found.

project: Loudermilk Center for Excellence and Blue Zone (east end zone)
note: Replaced Kenan Field House and enclosed the stadium: an academic center, Olympic sports strength center, visitors' lockers, and about 3,000 premium seats (capacity 63,000). Approved May 27, 2010 at $70M. Not football team space.

project: Kenan Football Center locker room and weight room renovation
note: About $5M renovation of the football locker room and weight room in summer 2019, after Mack Brown's return; the first floor was renovated in spring 2020. The figure comes from a search-result summary of these 2022 articles.

project: Football Sports Medicine Facility (Kenan Football Center addition)
note: 9,840 sq ft two-level addition to the Kenan Football Center: hydrotherapy with three pools and a training room with staff offices. Approved May 2021 at about $15M, funded by the Rams Club; work planned March 2022 to March 2023. Completion on schedule not confirmed.
An indoor stadium owned by the city on the NDSU campus. Ground broke Apr 26, 1990 and it opened in 1992 for $48M. Bison football has played there since 1993. The source does not describe team rooms.
A $1M air-supported dome over Dacotah Field. The first football practice in it was Dec 1, 2014. It was taken down for good in 2022 once the Nodak complex opened, so it no longer stands.
Twelve new LED displays in summer 2016 for $7.7M. Video only. A 2023 $131M remodel was rejected by voters twice.

project: Nodak Insurance Company Football Performance Complex
note: A $54M indoor practice facility for football that opened Oct 2022. Golf, soccer, baseball and track also use it. Groundbreaking year not found.

A 45,000 sq ft building opened in 2005 in two phases, the first piece of Mean Green Village. It holds the football coaches' offices, locker room and equipment room, plus sports medicine, the strength and conditioning center and athletics administration. Cost not found. A roughly $10M expansion (15,000 sq ft strength space, with a $4.6M Weger gift) won regents' approval in November 2025 for construction in summer 2026, so it is left out.

New stadium replacing Fouts Field; ground broke November 21, 2009, first game September 10, 2011. The estimate rose from $60M to $78M after the 2008 student vote. 30,100 seats, 21 suites, LEED Platinum. The source says nothing about team spaces.

project: Lovelace and McNatt Families Indoor Practice Facility
note: Ground broken September 29, 2018 and opened October 1, 2019, beside the Athletic Center off South Bonnie Brae Street. $16M (Denton Record-Chronicle), about half raised by athletics and half paid by the university; the Lovelace family gave $2.5M.
The east side was fully rebuilt in 1995 as a steel structure mirroring the west stands (HOK Sport). Seating. No cost given.

A $14M north end zone building. Ground broke fall 2006 and it opened Aug 2007. It has the football locker room, a 12,505 sq ft weight room, training room with rehab pools, 150-seat meeting room, video room, all ten coaches' offices and the equipment room. It also has an academic center.
Indoor facility opened Oct 2013: an 80,600 sq ft room with a full 120-yard field, plus the 6,400 sq ft Barsema Hall of Champions. Shared with baseball, softball and soccer. No cost given.

80-yard indoor field, the first step of a $30M 1996-97 football program (one listing says completed 1997). 14,400 sq ft extension completed 2003 (cost unknown). Rebuilt in 2019 as the Trienens Performance Center for other sports.
1996-97 renovation: field lowered about 5 ft, grass restored. Team-space work not documented. Demolished 2024.
Indoor football field, opened April 2018. Its cost is inside the combined Ryan Fieldhouse/Walter Athletics Center figure (next row).

Four-story center that serves all sports: academic support, nutrition and dining, sports performance, sports medicine and locker rooms for more than 500 student-athletes, plus offices for several varsity teams. Football's headquarters, with its own locker and meeting rooms. Groundbreaking November 13, 2015; opened August 1, 2018. The $270M is the combined cost with Ryan Fieldhouse ($220M early estimate).

35,000 seats. Demolition and construction from January 29, 2024; first game October 2, 2026. Budget $850M, raised to $862M ($875M in the infobox). team_spaces true assumes a new stadium includes home team areas; not specifically documented.

Gift of John R. Loftus; dedicated April 23, 1988; first football practice September 30, 1988. Holds Meyo Field (100-yard turf field), a track and an adjoining strength and conditioning facility. Football's indoor practice home until the Irish Athletics Center opened in 2019. Cost not found.

project: Notre Dame Stadium expansion (upper bowl, lights, locker rooms)
note: $53M, Nov 1994 to summer 1997: about 21,000 upper-bowl seats (80,795), permanent lights, a bigger press box. The home and away locker rooms doubled in size. Dedication game Sept 6, 1997.

96,049 sq ft football headquarters: staff offices, auditorium, weight room, training room, practice locker room, equipment room, meeting rooms. The university's groundbreaking release gives $21.25M. Ground broke November 2003; staff moved in July 2005.

About $400M: three 8-story buildings on the stadium (Duncan Student Center, O'Neill Hall, Corbett Family Hall) with premium seats, a media center and a south end zone video board. Started Nov 2014; first game Sept 2, 2017; finished Jan 2018. Academic, student and premium space, not team spaces.

111,400 sq ft indoor practice facility for football and soccer. Construction began in 2018 with a target before the 2019 season. Football first worked out there in August 2019. Cost was never disclosed.

project: Jack and Kathy Shields Family Hall
note: About 150,000 sq ft football operations building that replaces the Gug as football's home. Ceremonial groundbreaking April 20, 2024; unveiled July 31, 2026 before fall camp (footballscoop.com/2026/07/31). Cost reported as $100M or 'more than $100 million'; the university did not disclose an exact figure.

project: Peden Stadium north end zone grandstands
note: Two new north end zone grandstands; capacity to 19,000. Seating only.

Five-story west side tower added four years after 1986. Today it holds the press box, suites, football offices, athletic training, team meeting rooms, a recruiting lounge and the football locker room. Which of these were there in 1990 is not stated. Cost not found.

project: Carin Center (strength and conditioning center at Peden Stadium)
note: 10,000 sq ft strength and conditioning center added at Peden's ground level. Cost not found, so it may fall under the $3M bar. Probably shared with other Ohio teams.

project: Peden Stadium renovation (track removed, field lowered)
note: $2.8M after the 2000 season: track removed, field lowered 10 ft, Phillips Club seats, band seating, Victory Hill berm; capacity to 24,000.

project: Peden Tower football spaces renovation and expansion
note: Done after the 2004 season, early in Solich's tenure: expanded athletic training rooms, a large team auditorium, better position meeting rooms, a bigger recruiting lounge and more football coaches' office space. Cost not found and may be under $3M.

93,750 sq ft indoor pavilion next to Peden with a full football field and a running track. Varsity teams practice there, and campus recreation, ROTC and club sports use it too. Opened August 2014. Athletics and The Post give $12.5M, though other reports say $11.5M or $13M. $8M lead gift from Robert and Margaret Walter.

project: Perry and Sandy Sook Academic Center (Peden Stadium end zone)
note: 26,000 sq ft academic wing with a game-day hospitality room and an observation deck, finished fall 2018. The campaign also renovated locker rooms for other teams, not football. Listed as a stadium addition only; team_spaces false.
Dedicated November 1987. Indoor field (400x220x65 ft), weight room, training room, coaches' offices and meeting rooms. Original cost not found.
1998-2001: track removed, field lowered, new press box, 81 suites and 2,500 club seats; capacity 101,568. No team-space work found.
53,000 sq ft expansion, 2005-07 (two-story weight room double the old size). $21.5M per Wikipedia; Ohio State's own site says $19.5M.

project: Ohio Stadium south stands seating and permanent lights
note: About 2,500 south stands seats, permanent lights and waterproofing. $13.7M total; $8.9M for seats and lights alone.

project: Woody Hayes Athletic Center east wing renovation
note: Athletic Business lists $6.5M construction cost, occupied May 2019; a 2017 report put the planned project at $7.8M.

project: Ohio Stadium premium and infrastructure renovation
note: Announced 2016 as a $42M project planned for 2017-20 (removed about 2,600 seats). Completion year not confirmed. No team spaces.

project: Memorial Stadium south end zone seating with coaches' offices and training facilities
note: Wikipedia (citing OU's stadium history): improved south end zone seating with new coaches' offices and training facilities, added in 1980. Whether it included a locker room or weight room is not stated, so houses_football_ops is false. Cost not found.
Dedicated April 24, 1999: football offices, locker room, weight room, sports medicine. Demolished in summer 2015 and replaced by the south end zone project. Cost not found.
Full indoor field next to the stadium. OU says it opened in the 2002 season; Athletic Business lists occupancy March 2003 and a $9.86M construction cost.

project: Oklahoma Memorial Stadium east upper deck renovation
note: East upper deck with 2,500 club seats and 27 suites; capacity 83,469. The renovation cost $54M; the whole stadium project is also given as $75M.

project: Stadium south end zone and football facilities (Phase 1)
note: Approved March 2015. Enclosed the south end zone and rebuilt the Barry Switzer Center inside it: football offices, locker rooms, meeting rooms, training center and weight room (the 1999 Switzer Center was demolished in summer 2015). Seats opened for 2016; some reports date the new Switzer Center's dedication or completion to 2018-19. A $175M football operations building (approved 2023) had no confirmed groundbreaking.

project: Boone Pickens Stadium renovation ('The Next Level', incl. west end zone)
note: $260M upgrade, mostly Pickens money: a new west end zone, a brick exterior and a link to Gallagher-Iba Arena. Broke ground in the 2003 season; rededicated Sept 5, 2009, at about 60,000 seats. OSU athletics says football operations moved into the west end zone in summer 2009: football offices, position meeting rooms, strength and conditioning, locker rooms, equipment room and athletic medicine.

92,000 sq ft indoor practice building across from the stadium, plus three outdoor football fields (one turf, two grass). Plans unveiled 2007, opened June 2013. Sherman Smith gave $20M to endow upkeep.

project: Powhatan Sports Complex (now L.R. Hill Sports Complex)
note: 48,000 sq ft; built for the restart of football, shared with field hockey and women's lacrosse. Football offices and meeting rooms, locker rooms, lounge, a 6,000 sq ft weight room, athletic training, and 100- and 60-yard turf practice fields. Groundbreak August 2007, opened September 13, 2008.

project: Foreman Field renovation with the Ainslie Football Complex
note: New Ainslie Football Complex with the Monarchs' locker room, 24 suites and 400 lodge seats, plus visitors' locker rooms. Planned at $24.8M in 2007; the infobox gives $29,521,218. Ready for the first game, September 5, 2009.

project: S.B. Ballard Stadium reconstruction (Foreman Field rebuilt)
note: East and west grandstands demolished November 19, 2018, and rebuilt for the 2019 season; capacity 21,944. Sources don't say whether team spaces were rebuilt.

project: Vaught-Hemingway Stadium south end zone expansion
note: South end zone bowl with an upper deck, luxury boxes and club seats; about 10,000 more seats, capacity 60,580.
150,000 sq ft indoor practice and locker room facility with football offices, linked to the stadium by a tunnel. One report values it at $18M in 2004.

project: Vaught-Hemingway Stadium north end zone expansion
note: Forward Together phase 2: closed the north end zone, adding about 3,458 seats. Work ran Dec 2015 to Aug 2016. Figures differ: $33M (athletics list), $25.6M, $25M contract, $20M.
Began January 2022; team moved in late July 2023. Added 39,500 sq ft and a second story.

project: Autzen Stadium press box and suites renovation
note: New south-side press box; the old north press box became luxury suites.
102,000 sq ft athletics building at Autzen, opened September 1991; football's home until Hatfield-Dowlin (2013). Cost 'over $12 million'.
117,000 sq ft, the first indoor practice facility in the Pac-10. Groundbreaking March 1997, opened August 1998. $14.6M per a 1998 Emerald article (GoDucks: close to $15M).
South sideline seating and luxury boxes. The article text says $90M; its infobox says $80M.
145,000 sq ft, opened summer 2013. Early estimate $68M; the Oregon Daily Emerald reported closer to $138M. It began as the Knight-funded 'Casanova expansion', set to start construction in June 2011.
Sports science and performance space on the Casanova Center ground floor, for all sports. 'At least $19.2M' per the building permit. Opened late August 2016.
170,000 sq ft: a 130,000 sq ft indoor field plus a 40,000 sq ft connector to Hatfield-Dowlin. Ground broke February 2025; completion expected 2027. Donor-funded; no cost disclosed.
Finished behind the northwest end zone by the 1990 season. It holds a large weight room and football offices and meeting rooms. No cost given.

project: Parker Stadium grandstand roof and press box
note: Roof over the southwest grandstand approved in 1988; roof and new press box done in 1991. That grandstand was replaced in 2021-23.
New northeast sideline grandstand, with capacity from 35,362 to 43,300 for 2005. The infobox gives $80M for the 2005 renovation. The campaign began in 2003.

project: Raising Reser phase two (southeast end zone)
note: Built between the 2006 and 2007 seasons. It closed the horseshoe with corner seating and a video board, taking capacity to 45,674. No separate cost given.

project: Victory Through Valley (Valley Football Center expansion)
note: Announced Dec 2014 as $42M of upgrades to the stadium and Valley Football Center. Work was scheduled to start fall 2015 and was done for the 2016 season. It added an auditorium, coaches' offices, team room, locker room, rehab space and a hall of fame.
Unveiled Feb 4, 2021. Construction began Dec 1, 2021 and it was done for 2023; capacity is 35,548. No cost on Wikipedia, and team spaces are not described.
118,000 sq ft indoor facility. Penn State says built 1986 and named January 1987; other sources say completed 1987. Turf replaced 2003, 2012 and 2016 (each under $3M).

project: Beaver Stadium north end zone upper deck
note: Upper deck over the north end zone raised capacity to 93,967. No cost found.
About $14M. Penn State releases say it opened 1999; another account and a 2014 memo say 1998.

project: Beaver Stadium south upper deck and east suites
note: 10,000-seat south upper deck and 60 skybox suites. No team spaces.

project: Lasch Building locker room, equipment room and recruiting lounge renovation
note: Estimated $12M; designer approved January 2015 and plan unveiled August 2015. The 2016 completion year is inferred, not confirmed by a source.

project: Lasch Building renovation phase 1 (weight room addition, sports medicine)
note: Approved 2021 at $48.3M (part of a $69M plan from 2019). One report says completed late summer 2022; a board report says 2021.

project: Lasch Building renovation phase 2 (second-floor offices and meeting rooms)
note: Approved May 2023 with a $22M cap. Expected done by the start of the 2024 season; actual completion not confirmed. The athletic director put the whole multi-year Lasch program at about $98M.
106,000 sq ft bubble approved May 2023 with a $9.8M spending cap (one outlet estimated $5.2M). Substantial completion November 2025.
Approved May 2024; press box demolished January 2025. Completion targeted August 2027. Premium seating and 600,000+ sq ft of interior space; no locker room work found.

project: UPMC Sports Performance Complex (now UPMC Rooney Sports Complex), Panthers building and Duratz Athletic Complex
note: Shared with the Steelers: a 100,000 sq ft building split in half, with Pitt's half holding the weight room, training rooms, locker room, meeting and film rooms and coaches' offices. Built June 1999 to Sept 2000. The whole complex is reported at $30M to $80M, so the cost is left null.

project: UPMC Sports Performance Complex indoor practice facility
note: 125,000 sq ft with a full indoor football field. Four outdoor 80-yard practice fields too. Part of the same 1999-2000 build as the Panthers building, so no separate cost.

project: Heinz Field south end zone seating expansion
note: 2,390 seats and five suites in the lower south end (capacity 68,400), in place by summer 2015. Steelers project. Cost not found.
92,400 sq ft indoor field, plus football's weight room and offices until 2017. $10.3M; 1989 bids totaled $9.3M. Some sources date it to 1989.

project: Ross-Ade Stadium renovation phase I (Shively pavilion)
note: 2001-2003: new west pavilion with media center, 34 suites and club; concourse, restrooms, concrete and benches. Phases II and III were never built.
Groundbreaking April 15, 2016; opened August 2017, dedicated September 8, 2017.
Permanent lights for night games.

project: Ross-Ade Stadium south end zone renovation ("Your Ross-Ade" phase I)
note: About 4,500 south end zone seats, the student section and the Tiller Tunnel linking the Kozuch complex to the field. Work started after the 2022 home schedule.
AstroTurf replaced with FieldTurf, a new scoreboard, wooden bleachers replaced with metal benches, end zone seats tarped (capacity 47,000). Cost not found.

60,000 sq ft building forming the stadium's north end; construction began about July 2015 and finished in 2016 (a Houston Chronicle article from August 2016 is cited). It has the weight room, home locker room, and coaching and staff offices. The campus article's table lists 2017 as its construction date. Cost not found.

80,000 sq ft air-supported multipurpose bubble west of the stadium; approved May 9, 2019 and first inflated late July 2020. It hosts practices in bad weather and is shared with campus recreation. Cost not found.
New 41,500-seat stadium, groundbreaking March 9, 1993, opened September 3, 1994. team_spaces true assumes a new stadium builds home locker rooms; not specifically documented.

project: Rutgers Stadium expansion (south end zone, east mezzanine)
note: 968 club seats in 2008, about 11,500 south end zone seats in 2009. New locker rooms were deferred; a $5M donor-funded Brown recruiting lounge was added in the end zone.

project: Hale Center expansion and renovation (football headquarters)
note: Athletics says a $12.5M expansion (page undated). The new weight room was unveiled August 2016, inside a three-year phased renovation that also expanded sports medicine. 2016 is the weight-room year, not a confirmed finish.
Announced December 2016 and described as done in a September 2017 roundup. Replaced two 20-year-old turf fields; about 364,000 sq ft of practice space.

About 6,000 sq ft game-day locker room renovation, about $4M (the Browns' $4M gift), unveiled 2019. Linked to a board approval of up to $65M that mainly funded the Rodkin Academic Success Center (academic, so excluded).

project: Hale Center sports medicine and football recovery suite renovation
note: 22,000 sq ft, finished in 2022 per EwingCole: new sports medicine space and a football recovery suite (saunas, cryotherapy, float therapy) in the former lacrosse locker room. Part of a three-year phased Hale Center plan. It may overlap the $12.5M expansion row (2016). No cost found.

New on-campus stadium. Ground broke Sept 10, 1999 and it opened Sept 2, 2000. Its northwest corner connects to the Loyd All-Sports Center (lockers, training, offices), whose year and cost were not found, so team_spaces is false.

project: Gerald J. Ford Stadium premium seating and mini-suites
note: Extra luxury suites and Loyd Center infrastructure for outdoor seating. Announced 2012 and done for 2013. Cost not found.
Encloses the stadium's south end with a new football weight room, training rooms, meeting rooms and offices. Ground broke Dec 2, 2022 and it was dedicated Sept 6, 2024.

Broad Athletic Facility: home of Hornet football and track and field, with offices, locker rooms, athletic training room and weight room. Football and track moved in spring 2008. About $11M, $2M of it from Eli and Edythe Broad. A Nov 2007 report gave $8.9M instead. The 2006 and 2007 reports disagree on when construction started, so groundbreak is left null.

New on-campus stadium replacing Pritchett Field; ground broke 1985, opened Sept 13, 1986. The university's building name, Elliott T. Bowers Stadium and Fieldhouse, suggests the field house was part of it. Cost not given.
27,000 sq ft football field house at Bowers Stadium; interior and exterior renovation worth $11,667,000, expected to finish Oct 2021. Wikipedia words the finish date as expected, not confirmed.

project: Bowers Stadium field renovation (new turf, track removed)
note: Turf replaced and track removed in 2024 (construction under way in June 2024). Cost not found.

project: Bowers Stadium renovation (new five-level press box and concourse)
note: $60M approved by the regents Aug 2024: a 60,000 sq ft press box, covered concourse with club seating, fan shop and concessions. The team played 2025 at Shell Energy Stadium in Houston during construction (exact groundbreaking date not found) and is back at Bowers for 2026. Fan areas only.
City stadium shared with the Chargers. The 1997 project enclosed the stadium and added nearly 11,000 seats (to 70,561) for Super Bowl XXXII. Not an SDSU project. Demolished 2020-21.

project: Fowler Athletics Center (opened as Aztec Athletics Center)
note: Athletics headquarters: a 13,000 sq ft weight room on the first floor, coaching offices on the fourth floor, and the football team's Don Coryell Locker Room. Reported as a $13M complex nearing completion in May 2001; the formal opening may have been early 2002. Renamed for the Fowlers in 2011 after a $5M pledge. Football's daily home even after Snapdragon Stadium opened.

project: Don Coryell Locker Room renovation (Fowler Athletics Center)
note: Football locker room refurbished over about six and a half months and unveiled Aug 6, 2018. Cost not found and may be under $3M.
SDSU's own 35,000-seat stadium in Mission Valley. Ground broke Aug 17, 2020; first game Sept 3, 2022; cost $310M. Shared with MLS and NWSL soccer. Football team rooms are not described in the source.
In the 1980s, end zone bleachers, an upper deck and west side boxes took capacity from about 18,000 to over 31,000. The infobox gives $2.25M for the 1985 expansion.

project: CEFCU Stadium north end zone video board
note: A new video board and bar area where the north end zone bleachers stood. The Spartans article says it was installed in 2021 for about $5.2M; the stadium article says it was finished in 2020. Video and fan space only.

A 55,000 sq ft east-side addition finished Aug 2023: football operations center, locker rooms, offices, meeting and training rooms, sports medicine. It also holds soccer offices and lockers, dining and premium areas. The stadium article gives about $70M; an older passage gives a projected $57.6M. About 9,000 seats came out in 2019 for it. Groundbreaking year not found.

49,000 sq ft: an 8,000 sq ft weight room, coaches' offices, locker room, training room, team and position meeting rooms and a players' lounge. Athletics says it took about a year to build and was finished in August 2009. No cost found.

96,000 sq ft covered practice facility, opened just before the 2018 season (Aug 3, 2018). Construction began spring 2017, the frame collapsed in July 2017, and work resumed January 2018. WPMI called it an $8 million facility. No final cost confirmed.

New 25,450-seat on-campus stadium replacing off-campus Ladd–Peebles. Construction started August 6, 2018; opened September 12, 2020. Listed features are suites, loges and boards; the team's own spaces stay in the nearby fieldhouse.

project: Jerri and Steve Spurrier Indoor Practice Facility
note: $14.3M, opened 2015 at the west end of Gamecock Park next to the outdoor practice fields.

project: Cyndi and Kenneth Long Family Football Operations Center
note: 110,000 sq ft. Construction began March 2017; occupied January 2019. Athletic Business lists a $42.53M construction cost.

project: Williams-Brice Stadium 2001 Club and gameday upgrades
note: Approved 2019 for the 2020 season. Glass-front premium club in the southwest corner where the team enters, plus restrooms and concessions.

First of three phases of a $350M (later $356M) premium-seating renovation. Phase 1 (about $100M) ran late Nov 2025 to Aug 2026. Phases 2-3 (about $250M) start after the 2026 and 2027 seasons and finish by 2028.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers' NFL stadium, 13 miles from campus, and USF's home field until the on-campus stadium opens in 2027. Ground broke October 15, 1996, opened September 20, 1998. Its later $100M+ renovations were the Buccaneers' work and are not listed.

104,000 sq ft athletics headquarters, opened 2004. It has the main strength and conditioning center, sports medicine clinic, coaches' offices, and locker rooms for football and other sports. It was football's main home before the 2022 indoor facility. Cost not found.
Three full fields (two natural grass, one FieldTurf) plus a 40-yard turf drill area.

88,000 sq ft building with a 100-yard indoor turf field at the Morsani complex, plus football team spaces. Construction began September 2021 and finished November 2022; grand opening January 10, 2023. More than 500 donors gave $22M for it; the $5.1M Porter family gift named it. A $40M figure in one outlet refers to a broader 2017 football-center plan.

About 35,000 seats. Official groundbreaking was November 8, 2024 per the program article; another passage says late 2023. Earlier cited at $340M. The updated budget approved April 29, 2025 ($348.5M) includes expanded academic spaces and locker room upgrades, hence team_spaces true. Opening set for the 2027 season.

project: M. M. Roberts Stadium rebuild (now Renasant Stadium)
note: Rebuilt 1974-76 with double-decked east and west grandstands (33,000 seats); the team played all of 1975 away. Rededicated September 25, 1976. No team-space details.

project: Roberts Stadium press box and west-side renovation
note: New press box and president's box, chairback seats on the west side, field irrigation. Not team spaces.

project: Southern Miss Athletic Center, now Jim and Thomas Duff Athletic Center (north end zone)
note: Field house and athletics training building in Roberts Stadium's north end zone, opened 2002. Football moved into its training room, locker room and weight room in July 2002. The athletics facilities page calls it the '$11 million Athletic Complex', paid for by private donors. Renamed for the Duffs in 2012.

project: Roberts Stadium south end zone enclosure
note: Nearly 4,000 seats and 33 suites in the south end zone, east-side club level, elevators and a new north scoreboard. It also added a visitors' locker room, which is not the team's own space.

project: Stanford Stadium renovation before Super Bowl XIX
note: Over $2M, much of it from the NFL: press box renovated, new locker rooms, ticket complex, officials' room, more restrooms. Done for the Jan 1985 Super Bowl. Below the $3M guide, but stadium work since 1984 counts.
Wider concourse, better restrooms, the last wooden seats replaced. Paid for by a $10M gift announced Feb 1994; the $10M is the gift, not a confirmed final cost.

Rebuilt right after the Nov 26, 2005 game as a 50,424-seat concrete stadium with no track. Opened Sept 16, 2006. Wikipedia does not say whether team spaces were rebuilt, so team_spaces is false (unconfirmed).

project: Arrillaga Family Sports Center football addition
note: Football wing added to the athletics building, opened 2013: locker room on the main floor, coaches' offices and eight team meeting rooms above, and an expanded weight room and training center below. Fox Sports reported $21M; trustees approved $17M in Nov 2011. Football's old space in the building went to other sports. The opening year and cost of the original Arrillaga Family Sports Center were not found.
Replaced Archbold Stadium. Groundbreaking Nov 1978, building April 1979 to Sept 1980. The $26.85M includes a $2.75M naming gift (infobox: $25.63M). Team spaces not described, so false.

project: Manley Field House converted to indoor football practice
note: Once basketball moved to the Carrier Dome in 1980, the 1962 field house became an indoor practice space for football and lacrosse. It later got FieldTurf, glass windows and nearly a full-size field once its seats came out. Football's main indoor field until Ensley in 2015. Conversion cost and exact year not found.

project: Manley Field House football wing (Iocolano-Petty Football Wing)
note: New football complex on Manley with a Hall of Fame gallery at its center, designed by Lawrence C. Apgar. Dedicated Nov 3, 1991 and renamed for Iocolano and Petty in June 1996. Football's home until the 2025 Football Performance Center. Cost not found.
The air-supported roof was replaced in kind for $14M. A FieldTurf (2005) and video boards (2012) followed and are not listed.

87,000 sq ft indoor practice facility with a full FieldTurf field. Football is the main tenant and every team uses it. Announced Feb 2013 at $17M (the budget; no final cost found). Built in seven months, finished December 2014, named Jan 2015, and football's main practice facility from 2015.

project: Carrier Dome renovation (fixed roof, air conditioning, center-hung videoboard)
note: Announced May 2018 at an estimated $118M. The new roof was done Sept 2020 and air conditioning by 2021; full completion was expected in 2022. Not team space.

project: JMA Wireless Dome phase two (individual seats, event facility, digital upgrades)
note: Benches replaced with seats, a pregame event building and 5G and wireless upgrades. Began spring 2023, to be done before the 2024 season. The $45M is from the infobox, labeled '2022 renovations'.

project: Football Performance Center (Football Operations Center, Lally Athletics Complex)
note: New football operations building at the Lally Athletics Complex (the old Manley): locker room (the Michael M. Bill #59 Football Locker Room), coaches' offices, a team lounge, more sports medicine space and recovery rooms. Ground broke Sept 2023 and it opened April 2025. Part of a $150M Lally campaign that covers more than football; no football-only cost found.

Built in 1996 just outside the south end zone of Amon G. Carter Stadium for 'over $11 million'. It holds the sports medicine center, the football locker room, the weight room and the equipment room. Renamed the Walsh Physical Performance Complex in 2011; the Dutch Meyer complex was built on top of it in 2008, and it was refreshed in 2012. The sources do not say where the football offices are.

An indoor practice building of about 70,000-71,300 sq ft attached to Schollmaier Arena, with Cox Field. Announced June 2006 with $3M (Justin Foundation) and $4M (anonymous) gifts, $7M in all; dedicated May 10, 2007. The turf was redone in 2012 and 2022.

project: Dutch Meyer Athletic Complex and Abe Martin Academic Enhancement Center (2008 south end zone)
note: The 2008 suites and club seats are this $13M, 40,000 sq ft building on top of the Walsh complex in the south end zone. It opened Aug/Sept 2008 with 6 suites and about 255 club seats, plus a football team community room, a football meeting room and the athletics academic center. Football offices are not here, so houses_football_ops is false.

project: Physical Performance Center (Bob Lilly Physical Performance Center)
note: A two-story, 18,000-19,000 sq ft weight room for all of about 450 TCU athletes, dedicated October 14, 2011 (Justin Foundation gift). Football's weight room until the 2025 football performance center. Renamed for Bob Lilly in 2015. No cost found.

Announced Aug 2010 as a $105M west side and north end zone renovation. It grew into a rebuild of everything above the lower bowl, paid for by donors only, and was finished in 2012. It added a new 8,000+ sq ft football locker room for the 2012 season and refreshed the Walsh complex (summer 2012). Offices and the weight room stayed in other buildings, so houses_football_ops is false.

project: Amon G. Carter Stadium east side expansion
note: The article text gives $118M, while its infobox gives $100M (2020 east side expansion). It added suites and club seats. The source does not say whether it added team rooms.

project: Human Performance Center expansion and renovation (incl. Harrison Family Football Performance Center)
note: Announced Dec 2022 at about $40M (lead gift of $10M from the Justin Foundation) and grown to $50M from donors. Construction began January 2024, with July 2025 completion; it was shown in Sept 2025. It includes the Harrison Family Football Performance Center (20,000 sq ft football weight room and team space), a modernized Bob Lilly center and the Simpson Family Restoration and Wellness Center for all 22 sports. No football-only figure, so the whole $50M is here.

Temple's football building and practice complex on the main campus, dedicated December 9, 2000. It holds the team and coaches' locker rooms, the weight room, the training room, equipment rooms and coaches' offices. George Edberg-Olson gave $1M of an estimated $7M construction cost. Temple has no indoor practice facility found.
The Philadelphia Eagles' NFL stadium; Temple's home since 2003. Ground broke May 7, 2001, opened August 3, 2003. The 2013–14 renovation was the Eagles' work and is not listed.

Approved Oct 2011 at $9M; the final figure was $10M, finished mid-2012. A 15,000 sq ft addition: the weight room went from 2,500 to 10,000 sq ft, plus hydrotherapy pools, a bigger sports medicine office, an academic area, a 3,500 sq ft team function room, a renovated team meeting room and a remodeled locker room.
Opened July 15, 1989: 120,000 sq ft football building with a 70-yard indoor field, later lengthened to 100 yards by the 2012-13 Lawson/Anderson addition.
Closed in the upper level for a net gain of 10,642 seats. Cost not found.

project: Neyland Stadium master plan Phase I
note: East club seats, north concourse, LED signage.

project: Neyland Stadium master plan Phase II
note: Renovated the Peyton Manning Locker Complex and its tunnel, added the Lauricella Center and a media room, and redid the west concourse.

project: Neyland Stadium master plan Phase III
note: West club seats, suites and press box upgrades, west side elevators, Gate 21 plaza.

project: Anderson Training Center (Brenda Lawson Athletic Center)
note: In use from fall 2012, dedicated April 19, 2013. With the Neyland-Thompson center it forms a 145,000 sq ft complex.

Budget $180M (2017), then $288M (2022), then $337M (2023). Premium seating and concourses. One report says work began right after the 2021 season; first parts were done before the 2022 season; completion targeted for 2026.
Built at the stadium's south end; houses the football locker room and weight room. Originally the Neuhaus-Royal Athletic Center; renamed in 1997.
52 suites and a club room; 3,959 more seats. Cost not found.

project: Indoor practice facility (the Bubble) at Denius Fields
note: Inflatable-dome indoor field, opened 2002. Replaced as football's main practice site by the 2026 Denius Texas Football Training Complex.

project: DKR Stadium north end zone expansion
note: Demolition began Dec 8, 2006. Upper deck, suites, clubs, athletics offices and academic space.

project: DKR Stadium improvements with Football Academic Center
note: A $27M UT System project: a new Football Academic Center, a new Hall of Fame, FieldTurf, and 4,525 permanent south end bleachers. Most of it is not team space; the academic center is the team part.

Summer 2011: the player locker room was renovated with 135 new wide lockers, an exhaust system, a nutrition bar, a gaming lounge and LED screens. UT's 2013 facilities page also lists a new training room, players' lounge and a near doubling of the strength area among recent Moncrief-Neuhaus upgrades. Its own cost was not found.
Locker room, weight room, meeting rooms and training room, March-July 2017. Press reported $10M; a state filing estimated $7M.

project: DKR Stadium south end zone and Moncrief-Neuhaus overhaul
note: Ground broke May 4, 2019; the team moved in August 2021. Enclosed the south end and overhauled football's coaches' offices and team areas. Announced at $175M; Wikipedia's infobox gives $200M.

project: Frank and Wofford Denius Texas Football Training Complex
note: Indoor and outdoor practice complex on the old School of Social Work site next to the Moody Center. Construction began June 2024; unveiled before the 2026 opener. About $70M in pre-construction reports.

project: Kyle Field Bernard C. Richardson Zone
note: North end zone, over 20,000 seats; capacity 82,600.
Finished fall 2003 at the stadium's south end: players' lounge, locker rooms, training and rehab, academic center. Cost not found. A $52M renovation starts after the 2026 season, so it is not listed.
Multi-sport indoor facility with a regulation football field, about 208,200 sq ft. Football scrimmaged inside in Aug 2008. Occupancy listed Dec 2008; some sources say 2007.
Locker rooms and coaches' offices. Approved at $16M-16.8M in early 2014; the completed total was later reported as $20.8M.
$485M approved May 2013; started Nov 2013 and finished for 2015 at $483.9M. Capacity 102,733. No team-space rebuild confirmed, so team_spaces is false.

A $17.1M redevelopment of the football building's second floor, December 2022 to August 2023, funded through the Centennial Campaign (including a $7.5M Wayne Roberts gift). It did not include player spaces: the staff and meeting areas were redone. A further three-phase $52M renovation starts after the 2026 season and is not listed.

About 132,000 sq ft indoor fieldhouse; replaced McFerrin for football. Opened late summer 2023. The A&M System's vice chancellor put the first sub-project (indoor football center plus two outdoor football fields) at $72.4M, inside the $235M Bright area development. Construction started about June 2022 (WTAW). Includes a $15M Coolidge gift.
Ground broke 1979 and it opened in 1981. No cost given.
South end zone building, finished and dedicated in 2002. It houses football operations, a full-service training center, meeting rooms and coaches' offices. No cost given.

project: Jerry and Linda Fields West Side Complex
note: Three-tier addition to the home side with 450 club seats and 15 suites, done for 2009. Donor-funded, cost not given. Premium seating only.

project: Bobcat Stadium north end zone expansion
note: A $33M expansion that closed in the north end zone, taking capacity to 30,003 for the first FBS season. Team spaces not described.

project: South end zone club and seating
note: A new south end zone club and seating opened in 2025, with capacity at 28,388. The article does not say whether it replaced or rebuilt the 2002 End Zone Complex team spaces, and gives no cost.

project: West side press box and West Stadium Club
note: 175,000 sq ft press box with suites, club seats and camera decks; added 2,000 seats. Finished during the 2003 season and largely funded by SBC.

Football's home before the 2025 Womble Football Center: athletic training, strength and conditioning (a weight room of about 6,500-10,000 sq ft), nutrition, coaches' offices and the locker room. A search summary dated it to 2004 (not confirmed in a page I read in full). The lobby was redone in 2009, and the locker room got a $1.6M remodel in 2017 (below the $3M line, not listed). No cost found.

project: Northeast and northwest end zone seats (2009)
note: 6,100 general admission seats opened Oct 24, 2009. Seating only. Cost unknown.
Spanish Renaissance east facade, 1,000 general seats, 550 club seats and 26 suites. Groundbreaking Nov 29, 2008, finished 2010.
368 seats, an observation deck, a large video board, a colonnade and a north concourse. Began Jan 2013, finished Nov 2013. The stadium article says $16M; the athletics article says $11M.

project: Sports Performance Center (Petersen Family Indoor Football Practice Facility)
note: Football's indoor practice field (used from August 2017 camp) and an indoor track competition venue with 1,500 seats, under one roof; opened October 2017. The university budget and KTTZ give $48M, while the state licensing record and Flintco give about $38M. It is multi-sport, so the whole cost is here.
Rebuild of the outdoor football practice fields next to the Football Training Facility and the new indoor field, begun Feb 2018. Roughly $2.4M per the search summary of the release.

project: South end zone project (Dustin R. Womble Football Center)
note: South end zone building with premium seats, plus the Womble Football Center for the team (locker room, a 15,000 sq ft weight room, offices and meeting rooms). Construction began Nov 27, 2022, and the football center opened March 5, 2025. The $242M total covers both parts (Amarillo Globe-News via Yahoo); estimates were $200M in 2022 and $220M in 2023. No final football-only figure exists.

project: Glass Bowl expansion and Larimer Athletic Complex
note: Upper decks on both sidelines, three-story press box, 45 suites, Stadium Club, and the Larimer Athletic Complex (football's locker, meeting and weight rooms and offices, shared with the athletic department). Text gives $18.5M, infobox $18M. The program article lists Larimer in use from 1991.
Indoor multi-use athletics building with a 100-yard FieldTurf field, in use since 2010. Cost and groundbreaking not found.

$3.5M: new turf, facade, concessions, restrooms, locker rooms, ticket booths. team_spaces true only because locker rooms are named; whose locker rooms is not stated. Groundbreaking 2016 comes from the title of the linked UT News story (April 2016).
Listed only in the infobox cost list ($15M, from the 2022 media guide); what it built is not described, so team spaces are unknown.

project: Veterans Memorial Stadium west upper deck
note: Upper deck on the west side (12,000 to 17,500 seats) and a new scoreboard. Partly funded by Richard Scrushy.

project: Veterans Memorial Stadium expansion and six-story press box tower
note: East grandstand rebuilt, track removed, capacity to 30,000. The new tower has sky boxes, a club, and floors for sports medicine, academics, and strength and conditioning. The infobox lists it as the '2002 renovation, $18M'; the text says 2003.

project: Veterans Memorial Stadium video board and ribbon board upgrade
note: Infobox lists a $8.5M 2014 renovation; the text describes a south end zone video board, ribbon boards and sound system only (text marked citation needed).

project: North End Zone Facility at Veterans Memorial Stadium
note: Groundbreak November 12, 2016; finished 2018. Strength and conditioning and nutrition on floor 1; locker room, sports medicine, team lounge and plunge pools on floor 2; coaches' offices, meeting rooms, video and a recruiting lounge on floor 3. Also 402 club seats and a 3,150 sq ft video board.

Finished in 1990 for about $7.2M. It holds all of football's on-campus spaces: training room, weight room, equipment room, locker and meeting rooms, academic support and football offices. It sits at the north (Wilson) end zone of Yulman Stadium. Later work (2006 re-opening, the $1.2M Slatten strength center, the 2024-25 atrium) has no cost at or above $3M.

New on-campus stadium replacing the Superdome as home; ground broke January 28, 2013, opened September 6, 2014. 30,000 seats including 4,500 club seats and a large year-round meeting space. The source does not mention football locker rooms or offices.

Announced Feb 11, 2025 and opened Feb 24, 2026, so it was built in 2025. An air-supported cover rising 60 ft over a field of about 75-80 yards, between Turchin Stadium and Claiborne Avenue. For football and all 17 sports. No official cost; a $42.069M figure in the student paper is satire.

A three-story, 29,000-30,000 sq ft football building in the north end zone of the stadium, where the north stands came down in Feb 2005. Ground broke Oct 2005; digging began Jan 2006; it opened June 2007 (one source says Sept 2007). The 2020 yearbook gives $10M; Athletic Business lists $7.8M of construction. Named for Mike Case. Tulsa has no indoor practice facility (plans were shelved in 2016).

project: Skelly Field at H. A. Chapman Stadium renovation
note: 2007–2008 renovation (the project was underway when the stadium was renamed in April 2007; the main work came after the 2007 season). New seating, press box, club and loge seats and scoreboard; the west upper stands were removed (capacity about 30,000). Cost not found.
80,000 sq ft open-air covered practice pavilion; roofed but not enclosed. Its $4.2M is part of the $22.5M operations center project.

46,000 sq ft football operations center with an outdoor turf practice field; ground broke August 29, 2016, opened August 18, 2017. The $22.5M covers the whole project, including the $4.2M Legacy Pavilion (separate row; do not add twice).

Opened August 2003 for $5.2M. It is the home of UCF football (offices, locker room, players' lounge) and holds the athletics department's main sports medicine and strength and conditioning rooms. Nicholson Fieldhouse was added behind it in 2005.

Indoor practice field behind the Wayne Densch Sports Center and the first indoor practice field among Florida's FBS programs. A 2004 UCF release projected $4.3M (the Nicholsons gave $2M). It was finished before the 2005 season (June 2005), not in 2007.

project: Bright House Networks Stadium (now Acrisure Bounce House)
note: New on-campus stadium, broke ground March 22, 2006, first game Sept 15, 2007; it replaced the Citrus Bowl. Gameday team rooms not confirmed in the sources.

project: Stadium renovation with Wayne Densch Center for Student-Athlete Leadership
note: $8M after the 2014 season: the student-athlete leadership center (academic and leadership use) on the east facade and an east party deck. No football team rooms.

project: Wayne Densch Sports Center renovation (Hagle Football Gateway)
note: A full interior renovation of the Densch center: sports medicine and performance, an expanded football locker room and players' lounge, student spaces and new HVAC. The Board of Governors list gives $20,255,188. Part of the $60M Hagle Football Gateway, begun April 17 (2024 by the reports); finishing touches and the promenade were done for the 2025 season. A final completion date is not confirmed.
West tower about 2.5 times larger: suites, club seats, press box and broadcast booths. Work began Dec 2024 and finished Aug 2026, in time for the 2026 season. Premium seating only.

Training room, strength room, varsity locker rooms and the Bud Knapp Football Center; football's main home until 2017. 2003 report: $14.23M with completion projected January 2004; UCLA's page says remodeled 2006.
Budgeted at $152M in 2010, rose to about $170-177M; mostly done 2013. Terry Donahue Pavilion with press box and suites. City-owned stadium UCLA leases; the locker-room work was separate and earlier.
75,000 sq ft next to Spaulding Field. Groundbreaking August 27, 2015; grand opening August 1, 2017. Cost cited as $50M (2015 estimate), $65M (fundraising target) and $75M (LA Times).

project: Pratt & Whitney Stadium at Rentschler Field
note: New state-owned stadium in East Hartford; ground broke Oct 21, 2000, opened Aug 30, 2003, $91.2M. Team spaces here are only the game-day locker rooms; the daily home is the Burton complex in Storrs.

Coaches' offices, team meeting rooms, video rooms, dining hall and lounge, built together with the attached Mark R. Shenkman Training Center (85,000 sq ft indoor field and 18,000 sq ft strength center) as one 165,000 sq ft project. Construction began fall 2004; opened July 2006. The $57.9M covers both buildings; the Shenkman center is listed only here so it is not counted twice.

project: Malone Stadium (now FMOL Health/St. Francis Stadium)
note: Opened September 16, 1978, with 20,000 seats. The lower west stands enclose the ULM Athletic Training Center, but sources don't say whether that was original, so team spaces are left false.
8,350 seats added, capacity to 30,427 (the press box was also enlarged in 1991). Seating only.

project: ULM football field house (north end zone)
note: 11,750 sq ft, finished August 2016, attached to the west grandstand. Locker room, coaches' offices, hall of fame and patios.

project: Football Performance Center and press box complex (McGuirk Stadium)
note: North end training facility and locker rooms, plus a new two-level press box with suites; estimated $20M, finished at $34.5M (the cost covers both parts). Work began March 2013, ceremony April 26, 2013; staff and players moved in July 2014.
Built for $3.5M and opened Oct 23, 1971. UNLV's home through 2019. It closed Dec 2020 and Clark County bought it. Team spaces not described.
Renovated in 1999 (Ellerbe Becket), with capacity up from 32,000 to 36,800. No cost given for 1999. A $1.2M renovation in 2015 is below the threshold and left out.

A $34.8M on-campus football complex that officially opened Oct 2019. A $10M Fertitta gift in Sept 2016 funded a 73,000 sq ft football facility. The UNLV Rebels article calls it the largest football practice facility in the country. Groundbreaking year not found.

The Raiders' domed stadium, which UNLV shares (first Rebels game Oct 31, 2020). Ground broke Nov 13, 2017. The $1.9B cost is the whole stadium, paid by the Raiders and county bonds, not by UNLV. It has an artificial turf field for UNLV. UNLV team rooms not described.

48,000 sq ft athletics building, $2.8M, opened 1971. Assumed football's office base before McKay (2012), not confirmed. Its $35M 2012-14 renovation served athletics administration, not football, so it is excluded.
Field lowered 11 ft and the track replaced with 14 rows of seats before the 1993 season.

project: Brian Kennedy Field addition to Howard Jones practice field
note: Practice complex expanded fall 1998. No cost found, so the $3M threshold is unverified. Brian Kennedy Field became the Bloom center site in 2024.

110,000 sq ft: football offices, meeting rooms, weight room, training room, locker rooms, plus the academic center for all sports. Groundbreaking January 2011; opened summer 2012. Football moved to the Bloom center in 2026.
Construction January 2018 to the 2019 season; estimated $270M, final $315M. New seats, press box/suites tower, video boards, concourses; capacity cut to 77,500. No team spaces listed.

About 160,000-165,000 sq ft with two outdoor practice fields, locker room, weight room, training room and meeting rooms. Groundbreaking November 7, 2024 (announced at $200M, later $225M); opened August 2026.

A two-story, 65,000 sq ft building beside the Sun Bowl that opened in August 2002. Larry Durham gave $5M toward the $11M cost. It holds the football coaches' offices (12 offices and a conference room), the football locker room and equipment room, and the athletics strength room (about 10,000-11,420 sq ft) used across sports. It is football's main home.
Announced Apr 2018 as a $15M project: luxury boxes in a new press facility, concourse renovation and west side premium seating. Done for 2021. Premium seating only.

project: Durham Center football locker room remodel
note: The first major upgrade to the 22-year-old Durham Center. Phase 1 (nearly $3M, new locker room with 115 lockers) was shown in August 2024; phase 2 ($2M, showers and restrooms) was planned for spring 2025. The $5M total covers both phases (lead gift from Jim and Julie Cardwell). UTEP has no indoor practice facility found.

City-owned domed stadium; ground broke November 5, 1990, opened May 15, 1993. UTSA's home since 2011. The city renovated it in 2008, 2009 and 2017 and added suites in 2006; none of that work was UTSA's.

Opened August 4, 2021 at Park West: football's home (offices, locker room, meeting rooms), plus athletics-wide strength, sports medicine and academic space, and two football practice fields (one turf, one grass). The final cost was $40.4M (with $10M from San Antonio's 2017 bond). The state licensing record shows construction began Nov 2019. The covered practice pavilion was cut to a later phase; UTSA has no indoor facility yet.

Rice Stadium was almost fully demolished after Nov 15, 1997, and rebuilt for the 2002 Olympics; it opened Sept 12, 1998, with 45,017 seats and a six-story press box. Estimated at $50M (Eccles Foundation $10M, Olympic committee $8M). Only the 1982 south stands were kept. Team rooms not confirmed.

74,000 sq ft indoor field, 60 ft high, built June to November 2004 for about $6M with private gifts (Spence Eccles gave $2M). Shared with baseball, softball, soccer, golf and track. A $61.8M football indoor facility was approved in Feb 2022, but no source shows it built by 2025, and its Guardsman Way site went to the new baseball park, so it is not listed.

project: Spence and Cleone Eccles Football Center
note: 150,000 sq ft, $32M (Utah Athletics, a Deseret News piece and an Aug 2013 Utah release; Athletic Business lists $24M construction cost). Football moved in July 2013 and the grand opening was Aug 15, 2013, on Guardsman Way. It replaced the Dee Glen Smith Center as the football home. Groundbreaking year not found.

project: Ken Garff Red Zone (south end zone)
note: Enclosed the south end zone: new home and visiting locker rooms (the home one 5,300 sq ft with 90 lockers), sports medicine, offices, premium seats and about 5,600 more seats. Announced 2019 at $80M (Ken Garff family $17.5M) and finished Aug 12, 2021. Groundbreaking date not found.

project: Jim and Carol Laub Athletics-Academics Complex
note: A 69,000 sq ft north end zone building that replaced the old complex torn down right after the 2006 season; finished 2008. It holds sports medicine, the equipment room, locker rooms, coaches' offices, meeting rooms, suites and an academic center. Not confirmed as football-only. No cost given.

A $6.4M, 21,000 sq ft weight room at the stadium's northwest corner. Ground broke May 26, 2012 and it opened late July 2013. It serves about 400 athletes from 16 sports and replaced a 5,800 sq ft room.

project: Maverik Stadium west side press box and suites
note: Demolition of the old west press box began Apr 2015, and the new building was unveiled Sept 1, 2016 for $36M. Four stories: press box, 24 suites, 24 loges, 700+ club seats and a club that also serves as the athletes' training table. Plus video boards and concourses.
Dedicated August 2002: two football practice fields and a weight room. Cost not found, so the $3M threshold is not confirmed.
Fences, ticketing building, east concourse, paint. Part of a $50M athletics upgrade that began July 2008.
West concourse, brick facade, entry plazas. The cost is an estimate.
North concourse, brick on the exterior, entry plazas. Estimated cost. The planned Phase IV north end zone football building (2011) seems not to have been built; a berm went up in 2012 instead.

project: McGugin Center football wing renovation (offices 2010, locker room 2011)
note: Football's offices in the McGugin Center (football's home) were renovated in 2010, and the football locker room was rebuilt and first used in June 2011. This was part of the 2008 five-phase upgrade; one phase was budgeted at $7-8M and included the McGugin football locker rooms (news.vanderbilt.edu, July 2008), but no cost is given for this work alone, so the $3M guide is not confirmed.
Full-length football field, shared with other sports. Opened November 2013. One source says $30M and 2014.

project: FirstBank Stadium north end zone (Vandy United)
note: Hospitality and loge seating plus the Huber Center basketball practice space. Done before the 2024 season. Its own cost is not given; part of the $300M Vandy United program.

project: FirstBank Stadium south end zone (Vandy United)
note: Football facilities, team dining and premium seating. Seats torn down spring 2023, blasting July 2023; opened for the Aug 30, 2025 opener. Its own cost is not given; part of the $300M Vandy United program.

Dedicated Sept 14, 1991, at 'over $10 million'. Holds football's offices, practice locker room and meeting rooms, plus an 8,000 sq ft weight room, training clinic and the AD's offices. Practice fields are behind it.

project: Scott Stadium expansion (upper deck and south end, Carl Smith Center)
note: Filled in the upper deck and south end for about 20,000 more seats, plus the pergola, lights and Hoo-Vision. The $25M comes only from the Wikipedia infobox and is not confirmed elsewhere. Video boards (2009, 2024) are not listed.

project: McCue Center restoration (football locker room refurbished)
note: Much of the center was restored in summer 2007, including a full refurbish of the football locker room and player lounge. Cost not found, so the $3M guide is not confirmed.

project: George Welsh Indoor Football Practice Facility
note: About 78,000-80,800 sq ft, about $13M from private gifts (one report puts UVA's full cost near $14.5M with loan interest). Opened spring 2013 and named for George Welsh in 2012. Groundbreaking year not found.

About 90,000-93,000 sq ft football operations center beside the Welsh indoor facility, $80M. Ground broke June 2022 (virginiasports.com 'UVA Football Celebrates Landmark Day'). Opened June 2024, when football moved out of the McCue Center.
Built and in service in 1998 and dedicated Sept 26, 1998, before the Pittsburgh game. It holds football's weight room and position meeting rooms (see the 2021 renovation). Cost not found.

project: Lane Stadium north end zone seating additions
note: About 2,100 seats in summer 1999 and 3,000 bleacher seats plus a Hokievision board in summer 2000. Cost not found.

project: Lane Stadium south end zone expansion
note: A two-deck structure with 11,120 seats enclosed the south end (capacity 65,115) before the 2002 season. Cost not found.

project: Lane Stadium west side expansion (press box, suites, club seats)
note: Built after the 2004 season: an 11,000-seat two-tier grandstand, 23 suites, press box, Hall of Fame, athletic fund and academic offices, and a new visitors' locker room. No home team spaces.
A nearly 42,000 sq ft, $18M building with the football locker room. The team moved in November 2010. Wrestling practices on its third floor. Groundbreaking year not found.

About 92,000 sq ft, 85 ft high, the most expensive indoor facility in the ACC when built. The Board of Visitors approved $21.3M (earlier estimates were $18M and $25M). Ground broke in 2014 (SI, May 2014, said it was about to) and it was finished in 2015. A $0.8M air-conditioning project was approved in 2026.

project: Merryman Center football weight room and meeting room renovation
note: Expanded the football weight room from about 6,900 to over 12,300 sq ft and updated and expanded the position meeting rooms for $4.5M (a 2018 report set a $5M target). The weight room was closed through the 2020 season and unveiled in March 2021.

project: Mark C. Pruitt Football Center (Peahead Walker Football Locker Room)
note: The football wing of the Manchester Athletic Center (built 1977), with coaches' offices, the team locker room and meeting rooms next to the Doc Martin practice fields. The Peahead Walker locker room was finished in 1988. It was football's home until coaches moved into the Sutton center (2019) and the locker room moved to the McCreary Football Complex (2023). Cost not found.

The 1968 field house behind the northwest end zone was torn down in early 1996 and rebuilt during the 1996 season, opening mid-1997. Wikipedia does not say what it holds, so team_spaces is false (unconfirmed) and the kind is uncertain.

Wake Forest Athletics says the football center was fully renovated in 2004 (coaches' offices, team locker room, meeting rooms). A later summer renovation of the Pruitt wing (110-locker room, offices, players' lounge; news.wfu.edu) has no confirmed year. No cost found for either, so the $3M guide is not confirmed.

project: Deacon Tower (new press box and premium levels)
note: Announced 2006. The old press box was imploded Jan 14, 2007 and the tower opened before the 2008 season. Part of a multi-phase renovation (brick facade 2005, FieldTurf 2006). Cost not found.

About 80,000-89,000 sq ft with 120 yards of indoor turf, $21M from private gifts (Bob McCreary's $12.5M lead gift). Opened Feb 2016. It was the first phase of a $58M project with the Sutton Sports Performance Center. Groundbreaking year not found.

A four-level, 87,000 sq ft building joined to McCreary Field House, opened Sept 13, 2019. It holds football's 10,000+ sq ft weight room and, on the fourth floor, 18,000+ sq ft of football coaches' offices and team meeting rooms, plus Olympic sports training space. Ben Sutton gave $15M. Its own total cost is not given; the field house and this center were a $58M two-part project, with $21M for the field house.

A 60,000 sq ft football addition joined to McCreary Field House and the Sutton center. It has the new locker room (replacing the 1988 Pruitt one), players' areas and recovery space. $38M from about 700 donors (Bob McCreary $20M). The ceremonial groundbreaking was Feb 12, 2022, with work already under way. Shown to the team late July 2023 (Athletic Business lists occupancy Nov 2023).
13,000-seat north grandstand; capacity 72,500. The roof collapsed during construction (February 25, 1987).
80,000 sq ft, shared with baseball, softball and soccer. Ground broke August 2000; opened September 2001. $28M per a Husky guide; a campaign table lists $26M.

project: Husky Stadium renovation with football operations center
note: Began November 7, 2011; reopened August 31, 2013. Built an 83,000 sq ft west-end football operations center (locker rooms, weight rooms, training, offices). Cost cited $250-280M ($261M at start).

Built on the Rogers Field site. In 1972 only the south grandstand, press box, lights and turf were new, for $1M; other sections were replaced later. The 1979 track removal is before 1984 and left out.

project: Martin Stadium phases I and II
note: Began at the end of the 2006 season and ran to 2008: north concourse, concessions, restrooms, a plaza and ticket office, and a scoreboard upgrade. Fan areas only, no cost given.
An $80M south side building: press box, 21 suites, 42 loge boxes and about 1,300 club seats. It began Nov 2011 and was done for the 2012 opener. Premium seating only.

A $61M football operations building in the west end zone: weight room, locker rooms, equipment and training areas, meeting rooms, coaches' offices and a heritage area. Construction began Nov 26, 2012 and it was done for the 2014 season. The budget also covered new FieldTurf.

Built in 1980 south of the stadium for football offices and connected to the stadium in 1985. About 39,000 sq ft with the locker room, training facilities, a 23,000 sq ft weight room, coaches' wings, meeting rooms and position rooms. Cost unknown.
New 50,000-seat stadium on the Evansdale campus. Groundbreaking May 3, 1979, opened Sept 6, 1980. The football offices were in the separate Facilities Building row.

Enclosed the south end zone bowl and connected the Puskar Center to the stadium. The stadium article says 7,500 seats for $6.5M; the football article says 11,000 seats. A $650,000 north end addition followed in 1986.
The stadium's first 12 suites, in the front row of the west press box. Premium seating only. Cost unknown.
Opened Aug 1998: a 90-yard FieldTurf field with more than 75,000 sq ft of practice room. The Antoline outdoor fields are behind it. Cost unknown.
18 suites replaced the north end zone general seats, and capacity fell to 60,000. Wikipedia marks the $13M as citation needed. The terrace was enclosed with 180 more seats in 2007.

project: Puskar Center and locker room renovations (2012-13)
note: Weight room, interior, player lounge, coaches' meeting areas and the locker room renovated in 2012 and 2013, before the 2013 season. Cost unknown, so it may be under $3M.
New 162-seat team meeting room, announced in spring 2014 and finished in 2015. Cost unknown and possibly under $3M.
About $55M: the field crown removed with new drainage and turf (2016), east concourses, gates and box seats (2016), and the west concourse (2017). Fan side only.

project: Houchens Industries-L. T. Smith Stadium expansion and renovation
note: Renovation that raised capacity to 22,000 for the move to FBS. The infobox and WKU Athletics give $50M; early reports said $37.5M. Work began after the 2006 season and the ceremonial groundbreaking was in Feb 2007 (wkusports.com/news/2007/2/10). The final phase was the new West grandstand (over 5,000 seats), which also houses football's locker room, weight room, training room, coaches' offices, football operations and meeting rooms. WKU calls this the Football Complex, 'completed in 2007'; it was named the Harold and Juanita Koon Football Complex in Sept 2024. Houchens Industries gave $5M in July 2007.

project: Tim and Sarah Ford Fieldhouse (Hilltopper Fieldhouse)
note: WKU's first indoor football practice facility: about 120,000 sq ft, on the old football practice field between the stadium and Nick Denes Field. It is shared with intramurals, the band, esports and forensics, and holds a 21,000 sq ft baseball clubhouse. Regents approved it in June 2022 at $35M (budget; the final cost is not found, and the project also took in a new press box). Ground broke Nov 10, 2023 (wkusports.com/news/2023/11/10). Renamed Sept 2025 and dedicated March 24, 2026. An earlier $22M Med Center indoor complex was dropped in 2016.
Press box built in 1995 (the infobox also lists a 1995 renovation). Cost not found.

$25M, eight stories at the northeast end zone: indoor practice field (called the football team's indoor practice facility), weight and fitness rooms, staff offices, club suites; takes in the old Oakland Gymnasium.

project: Waldo Stadium and Seelye Center football upgrades
note: Almost $3.5M: new stadium turf, new indoor turf, a revamped weight room, remodeled locker room, renovated meeting rooms, a new team lounge.

project: Waldo Stadium scoreboards, video boards and sound
note: 2014-15 work brought the total since 2013 to $5.7M (infobox: $5.6M for 2013-2015), so this part was roughly $2.2M; no own figure given. Alec Gores gave $2M.

project: Stadium Club and President's Suite remodel
note: $3.6M premium space remodel in the 1995 press box, finished Sep 2024 and paid for by the WMU Foundation. Premium seating only.

80-yard indoor field plus football locker rooms, strength, sports medicine and academic space. Used from 1988; phase II handed over January 1989. Renovated as part of the 2014 performance center; its field is being replaced (2024- project).
Began December 2001 and concluded with the 2005 season. Added suites, club seats, a five-story office building and separate football program offices. Cost cited $109-110M.

project: Stephen M. Bennett Student-Athlete Performance Center (Camp Randall north expansion, McClain renovation)
note: Strength training, academic space, a football tunnel and renovated locker rooms. Broke ground January 2012; completed January 2014. Costs cited: $76.8M first pitch, $77.6M approval, $74M, $82M and $86M (UW campaign page).

project: Camp Randall south end zone (CR Future)
note: Construction from November 22, 2021, for the 2022 opener. 2,300 premium seats replaced about 6,000 bleachers; also new turf and press box updates. Post-completion report: 'more than $75M'.

project: Kellner Family Athletic Center (football indoor practice facility, Shell and McClain replacement)
note: Approved February 2024 ($285.163M). Replaces the Camp Randall Memorial Sports Center (Shell) and the McClain Center. Opened August 2026 as the Kellner Family Athletic Center. WMTV also calls it a home for all Badger sports; its kind is shared_athletics because it also holds men's tennis and serves every Badger sport, though most sources call it the football indoor practice facility. Later phases were planned through September 2027.

Construction began May 2000 and it opened Aug 31, 2001 for $9.4M. It is the training facility for all varsity sports and holds the football locker room, sports medicine and an academic center. The team runs from it to the field on game day.

project: War Memorial Stadium west stands and press box
note: In 2004 the west stands were refurbished and the press box expanded. No cost given.
Over 80,000 sq ft with a full-size field. Construction began fall 2006 and it was finished at the end of 2007 for $11M, from donors and state matching funds.

project: War Memorial Stadium Wildcatter Stadium Club and Suites
note: East side club with 12 suites and 256 indoor seats, opened before the 2010 season. The infobox gives "$50 million+" for the 2009-2010 upgrades, which may cover more than this club; the body gives no figure. Premium seating only.
Announced fall 2023 in two stages, spring 2024 and spring 2025, with capacity down to 29,181. The article does not say what was built or what it cost.
